summary: #363 — dev cloud runs queue instead of cancelling, and the shared bkit-auto-dev group can drop a different FID
description: cancel-in-progress is false for dev and true for feat/** and fix/**. bkit-auto-dev is ONE concurrency group for ALL FIDs: GHA resolves concurrency.group from trigger-payload context before the ctx step derives the FID, so it cannot be keyed on it. Two FIDs failing dev CI near-simultaneously can lose the older pending run to queue-collapse; the stale-run guard detects that and writes a dev-dispatch-dropped row to the job summary plus a ::warning::.
rationale: cancelling an in-flight /bkit-debug mid-run risks a half-written status.jsonl or a held worktree lock. A queued run re-checks the dispatch cap when it starts, so the same FID needs no manual re-trigger. The dropped-run record goes to the job summary rather than a committed status.jsonl because this branch is only reached once dev has advanced, so committing it would usually be a non-fast-forward and be lost in exactly the case it records.
alternatives: keep cancel-in-progress true on dev (cancels a running debug session); key the group on the FID (GHA cannot — the FID is not in the trigger payload); commit the dropped-run row to status.jsonl (non-fast-forward in the case it exists to record)

summary: A feature branch never bumps package.json version — the bump is the release procedure own commit
description: Feature work leaves package.json version and .bkit/version pinnedVersion untouched and adds its entry under CHANGELOG [Unreleased]. The bump, the managed-marker re-stamp and the CHANGELOG heading happen together in a chore(release) commit at release time.
rationale: stampManagedVersion reads package.json at install/upgrade, so a bump inside a feature branch re-stamps every managed file (176 here) to a version that does not exist yet. Merged to dev, that leaves consumers-facing markers advertising an unpublished version, and bkit check treats stale markers as a hard blocker on dev.
alternatives: bump in the feature branch as a forward-only release tag (what this branch originally did — reverted); bump on dev immediately after merge but before publish (same stale-marker window, just shorter)

summary: stats.jsonl stays as-is; the activity.jsonl rename/FID-reference proposal is rejected, not deferred
description: Design Addendum 3 § R (owner, 2026-07-27) reverses Addendum 2 § L: references: ["{FID}"] on outcome rows is rejected. .bkit/stats.jsonl and .bkit/friction.jsonl are HARVEST_COPY_FILES, copied wholesale into bkit cross-repo store; they must carry how bkit performs, never what a consumer is building.
rationale: A FID is consumer task detail; a cross-repo harvested store must not carry it.
alternatives: Split activity.jsonl (FID/summary/description-enriched outcome rows) out of stats.jsonl into docs/ — REJECTED (owner, 2026-07-25 then formally closed 2026-07-27): stats.jsonl is the hot file writeRollupShard drains into archive shards; durable consumer-legible history must not sit in a compaction path, and outcome rows must stay FID-free regardless of location.

summary: SUPERSEDED — the `__bkit__` envelope was removed by de-18 (deep containment)
description: `.claude/settings.json` and `.cursor/hooks.json` carry no `__bkit__` key. Ownership is declared by deep containment: `deepContains`, `writeTier2JsonContained`, `migrateLegacyBkitEnvelope` in `.bkit/src/bkit-tiers.ts`. `__bkit__` survives only as the legacy-migration advisory in `.bkit/src/bkit-preflight.ts`.
rationale: BAR-142 §A1 requires explicit verification that `__bkit__` doesn't clash with any Cursor-reserved key before implementing the Tier-2 deep-merge. Cursor docs (cursor.com/docs/context/rules) and `.cursor/hooks.json` schema at SchemaStore show no reserved `__*` keys. Claude Code's `settings.json` schema (`$schema: https://json.schemastore.org/claude-code-settings.json`) also has no `__bkit__` conflict.

summary: SUPERSEDED — the `__bkit__` envelope contract was removed by de-18 (deep containment)
description: `writeTier2Json`, `extractBkitNamespace` and `applyBkitNamespace` no longer exist; `writeTier2JsonContained` (`.bkit/src/bkit-tiers.ts`) replaces them with no envelope. The one clause that still holds: `detectHooksConfigOverwriteRisk` is deleted.
rationale: Tier-1 full-overwrite is unsafe for consumer-extensible JSON (KN-8). The `__bkit__` envelope gives bkit a stable, inspectable, rollback-safe ownership record without requiring comment markers (JSON has no comments). DELETE of `detectHooksConfigOverwriteRisk` is correct: the blocker was a stopgap — once Tier-2 deep-merge ships, the risk it blocked no longer exists.

summary: SUPERSEDED — transactional install via `.bkit-staging/` is not on the install path
description: Dispatch writes module files straight to their destinations and is NOT atomic across modules. `.bkit-staging/` is a per-run scratch area for rendered files only, cleaned by `discardAllStaging()` in a `finally`. `commitStaging` / `discardStaging` / `initStagingDir` ship as unused primitives. A mid-install failure can leave earlier modules' files written and `.bkit/version` unpinned; recovery is an idempotent re-run of `bkit install`, not rollback (`.bkit/src/bkit-install.ts` header, #255 P1-5). A real transactional path would be new work.
rationale: Prior to v0.9.0, a crash mid-install (e.g. `bkit-design-organise` lookup miss, BAR-141 regression) could leave partial writes in consumer dirs. Staging makes mid-failure the common case trivially safe: no staged file ever reaches a consumer destination unless the entire install succeeds.

summary: SUPERSEDED — the `setup-auth@v1` composite action was deleted (BAR-164)
description: `.github/actions/setup-auth/action.yml` and `.github/workflows/test-action.yml` are deleted. Consumers use the inline `env:` token block plus `pnpm config set` in `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/ci.yml`. The row body already recorded this reversal; only the envelope status was wrong.
rationale: The composite action encapsulates the PAT-shim boilerplate so consumers can reference a single `uses:` line. The bash fallback is kept because non-Actions CI consumers (e.g. CircleCI, Buildkite) rely on the env var pattern in the seeded workflow — removing it would break them without a migration path.

summary: SUPERSEDED — de-25 holds the current `/bkit-debug` loop contract
description: `DEBUG_MODE` is `NORMAL|SOAK` (no OBSERVE). Steps: 3 Run Tests, 5 Diagnose, 7 Soak. Counters are `NORMAL_ATTEMPT` / `MAX_NORMAL_ATTEMPT`; soak is bounded by `MAX_SOAK_ATTEMPT`, not `MAX_DEBUG_ATTEMPT`. Soak prompt is `.bkit/prompts/bkit-debug-failure-soak.md`. See `de-25-143-observe-mode-removed-observation-logging-folds-into` and `.bkit/workflows/bkit-debug.md`.
rationale: Reproduce, normal-fix, soak, and observe were four overlapping machines with two test-run steps and ~15 variables; build's loop proved one test-first Run-Tests head with a mode-selected fix step is enough. Folding observe into the loop is safe because Fetch Context already pulls the failing CI logs (observe no longer needs to re-run instrumented in CI). The `DEBUG_ATTEMPT` ladder makes the mode mostly derivable and the escalation legible (each invocation does more). Reusing the inner-loop counter as the shared budget needs no new constant. The in-loop NORMAL → SOAK escalation lives in the diagnose agent (not the orchestrator) because "is this localisable, or does it need iterative live-boundary soaking?" is a diagnostic conclusion — made at the right point (post-analysis) by the agent with the deepest context, and analogous to its existing STANDARD → PIVOT → FINAL escalation; the orchestrator owns the switch (diagnose recommends, orchestrator decides). Dropping `TEST_LIVE` follows from the unified loop: the only thing that needed a before-the-fact live check was Run Tests itself (it cannot list a non-existent turbo task), so that became an inline existence probe at Step 4, and every other consumer reads `TEST_SCOPE` post-run.

summary: SUPERSEDED — the seven-provider allowlist was cut to four
description: Current allowlist is `openrouter`, `ollama`, `opencode-zen`, `opencode-go` (`OPENCODE_PROVIDERS`, `.bkit/src/bkit-cli.ts`). `ollama-local`, `nvidia`, `groq`, `cerebras` are removed (asserted in `.bkit/src/bkit-cli.test.ts`); `zen` survives only as a hidden alias of `opencode-zen`. The zen managed-auth render path (no `{env:KEY}` block) is unchanged. See `opencode-provider-allowlist-cut-to-four`.
rationale: DE-27 shipped only `ollama-local` + `nvidia`; #245 stayed open to broaden coverage to the common OpenAI-compatible backends + opencode's own gateway. zen breaks the `{env:KEY}` block pattern (auth is opencode-managed), so it needs its own render + manifest-detection path rather than a seventh `OPENCODE_PROVIDER_DEFAULTS` row treated like the others. Cross-platform identity reuse keeps behaviour comparable across hosts. Probing live (not the docs page) caught a real drift — zen's docs listed `qwen3.7-plus`, the live endpoint only `qwen3.6-plus` (KN-40).

summary: SUPERSEDED — there is no cadence counter; the analysis block is refreshed on demand
description: `bkit.roadmap.buildCycles`, `bkit.roadmap.stalenessDays`, the `ROADMAP_CADENCE_FIRE` row and `.bkit/scripts/bkit-roadmap-cadence.sh` do not exist; the `package.json` `bkit` block has no `roadmap` key. The `roadmap-analysis` block is written only when a human runs `@bkit-utility-review-roadmap`; a phase close re-renders `roadmap-status` and carries analysis through untouched.
rationale: Anchoring on the last FIRE (a dedicated, rarer counter row) rather than the last refresh (a per-ship counter row) is the only anchor that can actually accumulate to threshold.
alternatives: Anchor on last analysis refresh — REJECTED: refresh fires every ship, so the count would reset every ship and the cadence would never fire. Ship-cycle count instead of BUILT-FID count — REJECTED (owner, 2026-07-27): a skipped ship should delay a fire, not lose one; counting builds (which accrue independent of ship cadence) achieves that.

summary: The /bkit-roadmap utility emits counter rows with workflow "roadmap", widening the documented jsonl workflow enum
description: Closing blocking gap 3 made /bkit-roadmap append a ROADMAP_SCAN_COVERAGE counter row. .bkit/jsonl.md documented the workflow field as design/plan/build/debug/ship — the five phase workflows — and the utility is none of them. Stamping a phase name would be a lie and would pollute per-phase telemetry summaries, so the utility stamps workflow "roadmap" / step "roadmap-refresh" and .bkit/jsonl.md was widened in the same change to document it. validate() in bkit-telemetry.ts enforces no workflow enum, so no code change was needed; a phase-filtered telemetry summary simply will not match these rows, which is correct.

summary: BAR-142 §A2 — .bkitignore public contract
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** `.bkitignore` is a new public file at the consumer repo root. Syntax: `#` comment, blank-line ignore, [picomatch](https://github.com/micromatch/picomatch) glob, optional `:dotted.key` suffix for per-key exclusion. Per-key is opt-in behind `BKIT_BKITIGNORE_PER_KEY=1` env var (off by default). Once shipped, the file and its syntax are a public contract.
- **Why:** Consumers legitimately override bkit-managed files (e.g. custom ci.yml jobs, additional `.claude/settings.json` hook events). `bkit check` currently reports false-positive drift for these. `.bkitignore` gives consumers a declarative escape hatch without touching the managed file itself. Per-key is opt-in because implementation cost is high and per-file covers the majority use-cases.
- **Discarded:** (1) Make per-key the default — implementation cost likely high; opt-in via env covers the primary use case. (2) Use a custom DSL instead of gitignore-style — picomatch is well-understood, has no shell-out, and is a pure-regex library (security: no injection risk). (3) Store in `.agents/.bkitignore` — consumer-owned files belong at repo root, not in the `.agents/` subtree (which is bkit-managed).
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-142 §A2, `.bkit/src/bkit-bkitignore.ts`, `docs/deferrals.jsonl` (per-key deferred)
rationale: Consumers legitimately override bkit-managed files (e.g. custom ci.yml jobs, additional `.claude/settings.json` hook events). `bkit check` currently reports false-positive drift for these. `.bkitignore` gives consumers a declarative escape hatch without touching the managed file itself. Per-key is opt-in because implementation cost is high and per-file covers the majority use-cases.

summary: #265 — Split `--tooling` into stack-agnostic `--ci` + opt-in `--typescript`
rationale: A non-Node repo could not adopt bkit's CI gate graph + prose-lint without inheriting `tsc`/`vitest`/`slop-scan`/`husky` it has no use for. Separating the agnostic foundation from the TS toolchain lets any repo install `--claude --ci` and stay green, while Node/TS repos opt into the full toolchain with `--typescript`.
description:
- **Category:** infra
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** Split the `--tooling` bundle into two composable flags. `--ci` = the stack-agnostic CI/quality foundation: the `ci.yml` **skeleton** (gate graph + capstone contract + branch-protection, with Node/TS step bodies shipped as commented examples) + Vale prose-lint config; **no `package.json` footprint**. `--typescript` = the Node/TS toolchain (`tsc`, slop-scan + `boundary/type-suppression`, prettier, husky + lint-staged) + the **wired** `ci.yml` step bodies; **implies `--ci`**. `--tooling` becomes a back-compat alias for `--ci --typescript`. Re-bucket module CONTENTS (not module IDs) to avoid dispatch/registry churn: Vale config `lint → ci`; `typecheck` + slop-scan helper scripts `core-walk → lint`. `uninstall --typescript` removes only lint + git-hooks (keeps the `--ci` foundation); `uninstall --tooling` stays symmetric (removes all three).
- **Why:** A non-Node repo could not adopt bkit's CI gate graph + prose-lint without inheriting `tsc`/`vitest`/`slop-scan`/`husky` it has no use for. Separating the agnostic foundation from the TS toolchain lets any repo install `--claude --ci` and stay green, while Node/TS repos opt into the full toolchain with `--typescript`.
- **Mechanism:** The wired `ci.yml` template is the single source of truth (bkit dogfoods it); the skeleton is **derived** by `deriveCiSkeleton`, which comments out every `# bkit:start ts-ci-steps … # bkit:end ts-ci-steps` region. `dispatchModules` sets `ctx.wiredCi = modules.has("lint")` so the `ci` module seeds wired when the TS toolchain is co-installed, skeleton otherwise. This guarantees the two `ci.yml` forms never drift.
- **Discarded — re-bucket module IDs / add bare `--lint`/`--git-hooks`:** maximises churn across the dispatch registry, resolveModules, detection, and the entire test suite for no user-facing gain (lint + git-hooks always travel together under `--typescript`/`--tooling`). Kept `lint`/`git-hooks` internal-only.
- **Discarded — maintain two hand-edited `ci.yml` templates:** guaranteed drift. The derive-from-wired transform keeps one source of truth.
- **Discarded — move the `lint:prose` npm script to `--ci`:** it is a `package.json`/Node convenience and `--ci` must stay package.json-free; only the Vale **config** (stack-agnostic) ships with `--ci`. `--typescript` always co-installs `--ci`, so a TS consumer still gets the config its `lint:prose` references.
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** #265, #263 (type-suppression rule prerequisite), DE-29 (#252 CLI surface redesign), `.bkit/src/bkit-cli.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-manifest.ts`, `.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts` (`deriveCiSkeleton`, `runCiModule`, `runLintModule`), `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/ci.yml`

summary: Claude + opencode cloud dispatch share one bkit-cloud.yml as two runtime-gated jobs
description: Both CI dispatch jobs live in a single `bkit-cloud.yml` template (`.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-cloud.yml`), which the consumer copies and owns, each independently gated on its own secret (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY for claude, OPENCODE_PROVIDER_KEY for opencode). One secret set means one job runs; both set means both run additively. The opencode job dispatches headlessly via opencode run, reading provider config from the committed .opencode/opencode.json, with the single OPENCODE_PROVIDER_KEY fanned out to every known provider env var name so the config {env:VAR} reference resolves whichever provider is installed.
rationale: one file is one audit surface and one template to copy. Runtime-gated jobs are idempotent — the second job is a near-instant no-op until the consumer adds its secret, so no consumer pays for a host they do not run.
alternatives: a separate opencode-cloud.yml file, or a separate CLI flag path treating the opencode host as a later phase — both double the template/audit surface for jobs that already no-op without their secret

summary: Recovered import edges are written into `graph.json` by one writer, `bkit-graph-repair.py`; every other graph script only reads the file
description: `bkit-graph-repair.py` is the only caller of `resolved_import_edges()` (`scripts/graphify/bkit-graph-imports.py:11-15`) and runs inside every `pnpm graph*` wrapper between `extract` and `cluster-only` (`scripts/graphify/bkit-graph-repair.py:8-9`). Each injected link carries `"_origin": "graph-repair"`; a re-run adds nothing. `bkit-graph-eager.py` and `bkit-graphify-rollup.py` read the graph and call `warn_if_unrepaired()`. Same in the template copies under `.bkit/templates/scripts/graphify/`.
rationale: When each reader re-derived the edges on read, there were two answers to which edges exist, and `collapse()` needed a subtraction whose only job was to stop double counting (the deleted header text in 14e2a557). Repairing on read also leaves `graphify affected`, `god-nodes`, `explain`, `path` and `query` on a graph missing those edges, because they read `graph.json` directly; `affected` is the one most likely to be trusted in a hurry, and a missing edge looks like a clean result (`scripts/graphify/bkit-graph-repair.py:13-21`).
alternatives: Repair on read inside each reader — replaced for the reasons above.

summary: The graphify example scripts scan source for drift, eager imports and routes, repair missing import edges into graph.json once, keep test code out of the pictures, and encode drift as one amber dash-patterned tint
description: `scripts/graphify/*` (template examples): bkit-graph-drift.py counts literal patterns over a product/tests partition with exact per-prefix budgets; bkit-graph-eager.py detects module-scope calls from source and counts downstream importers from graph.json; bkit-graph-surface.py joins routes to endpoints by literal scan with symbol-level attribution; bkit-graph-repair.py is the only writer of recovered import edges and runs before clustering on every graph-writing command; readers warn, never self-heal; bkit-graphify-rollup.py draws hue = called capability, dash + amber fill = any drift status, solid blue = budgeted, and keeps test code, eager findings and dead URLs off the diagrams.
rationale: External packages are not nodes in graph.json and graphify drops calls in module-level initialisers, so a duplicated mechanism or an import-time call is invisible to graph queries; a request URL is a string in a template literal, never an edge. Regex patterns like `new Ratelimit(` silently match nothing, which reads as clean. The test surface exists because test code is where guards live and a product-only scan cannot see inline `test()` statements; test helpers count as product because product-shaped code imports them. A surface walking zero files would pass every budget vacuously — the false green the script exists to prevent. Budgets downgrade a warning because one amber otherwise covers both an unbounded marker and a settled, CI-guarded count, and every sweep rediscovers the settled rows; an exact number with a reason and a two-way CI guard keeps it from hiding work. One repaired graph.json is the single source of truth so `graph:rollup` and `graphify affected` never disagree; a second on-read repair would need subtraction to keep two answers agreeing. Test-path rows are never painted because folder rollups smear one test row onto a whole package. One amber colour: no scan proves intent (a split can be deliberate, a bypass the one case the owner cannot serve, a dead URL a stub), so a ranked ramp would claim what the scans cannot support; dash patterns read in greyscale and for colourblind readers; emoji labels cannot be sized under GitHub's strict Mermaid. Budgeted rows still get a box because a budgeted bypass is still a bypass, and blue not green because green reads as `one`. Eager findings stay off the diagrams because hue and dash are already spoken for and the unit is per file, not per capability. The whole-repo graph.html (8.3 MB, ~9.8K nodes) renders as an unusable hairball. Mermaid edges under weight 12 are dropped because the module view is otherwise 322 edges. Reasons moved out of the script comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Graph-query drift detection — not adopted: cannot see external constructors. Brace-counting module scope — not adopted: template literals, regex and JSX unbalance it. Red/orange/yellow drift ramp — rejected: implies an unsupported ranking.

summary: The Renovate example opens PRs against `dev` and layers `dev`'s config over `main`'s
description: `.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5` sets `baseBranchPatterns: ["dev"]` and `useBaseBranchConfig: "merge"`. `useBaseBranchConfig` is itself read from the default branch, so it applies after one merge there.
rationale: bkit consumers gate `main` to PRs from `dev` only, so a PR Renovate opened against the default branch could not merge. Renovate reads its config only from the default branch; with `baseBranchPatterns: ["dev"]` and no `useBaseBranchConfig`, edits to `renovate.json5` on `dev` are invisible to Renovate and every config change would need a release to `main` before it took effect. Reasons moved out of the Renovate example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The Renovate example batches updates weekly, opens CVE PRs immediately on `dev`, and caps open and hourly PRs
description: `schedule: ["before 6am on Monday"]`, `osvVulnerabilityAlerts: true`, `prConcurrentLimit: 10`, `prHourlyLimit: 4` in `.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5`.
rationale: A weekly batch keeps PR noise low. OSV alerts give the same effect as Dependabot's `automated-security-fixes`, but the PRs target `dev` through `baseBranchPatterns`, so bkit branch protection accepts them. The PR caps stop a flood of major-version bumps from swamping the repo. Reasons moved out of the Renovate example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Dependabot `automated-security-fixes` — not used: its PRs target the default branch, which accepts PRs from `dev` only.

summary: The Renovate example never auto-merges prod minor bumps, majors, GitHub Actions or Docker base images, and sets `automerge: false` explicitly
description: Explicit `automerge: false` on the prod-minor, majors, github-actions and dockerfile rules in `.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5`.
rationale: Minor prod bumps ship new behaviour to users; a major bump needs a human to read the changelog; a workflow action bump can change CI behaviour; a base-image bump can shift the build toolchain. `false` is written out, not left absent, so the policy is greppable and an earlier matching automerge rule cannot silently flip it to true. Reasons moved out of the Renovate example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

references: docs/deployments.md § Renovate — fencing bkit's own footprint
summary: bkit's own Renovate config does not bump vite majors; vite stays on ^6 via root `pnpm.overrides`
description: `{ matchPackageNames: ["vite"], matchUpdateTypes: ["major"], enabled: false }` in `.github/renovate.json5` (bkit repo only); `package.json` `pnpm.overrides.vite` is `^6.4.2`.
rationale: vite 8 switched its default transformer to oxc, which fails transforming the bkit integration tests. Lift the hold when vitest supports vite 8. Reasons moved out of `.github/renovate.json5` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's own Renovate config does not bump pnpm majors
description: `{ matchPackageNames: ["pnpm"], matchUpdateTypes: ["major"], enabled: false }` in `.github/renovate.json5` (bkit repo only); `packageManager` is pnpm 10.
rationale: pnpm 11 is a config migration, not a drop-in bump: it ignores `pnpm.overrides` in package.json (they must move to pnpm-workspace.yaml) and blocks esbuild's build script by default (needs `onlyBuiltDependencies`), so it lands as a deliberate change, not a Renovate PR. Reasons moved out of `.github/renovate.json5` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The Linear → GitHub importer takes `GH_PROJECT_TOKEN`, then the keyring token (`gh auth token --secure-storage`), then plain `gh auth token`
description: `resolveGhToken` in `scripts/linear/linear-to-github-import.ts` (bkit repo only).
rationale: The keyring token typically has `project` scope; plain `gh auth token` may return an env-loaded fine-grained PAT that lacks it, and Projects v2 writes then fail. Reasons moved out of the script's comments and README (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The Linear → GitHub importer does not port the Linear project label (`cbartens/bkit`)
description: `LABEL_SKIPLIST` in `scripts/linear/linear-to-github-import.ts` (bkit repo only).
rationale: Linear models the project as a label; on GitHub the Projects v2 board already records the project, so the label would be redundant. Reasons moved out of the script's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit-cloud.yml keys concurrency per trigger surface; dispatch and the auto-ship it triggers never share a group
description: `concurrency.group` in `bkit-cloud.yml` is `bkit-auto-${{ inputs.issue || github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}`; races between a dispatched build and its auto-ship are handled by the orchestrator stale-run guard + status.json lock.
rationale: GitHub evaluates `concurrency.group` from trigger-payload context only, before any step runs. The dispatch payload exposes only the bare issue number; the workflow_run payload exposes only `head_branch` (`feat/{FID-with-slug}`). GHA expressions have no regex / split / replace-to-numeric, so stripping `feat/` yields `141-cloud-app`, not `141`, and the two tokens cannot be made identical. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's own CI cancels superseded runs only on pull_request, never on push to main/dev
description: `concurrency.cancel-in-progress` in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (bkit repo only) is `${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}`; push runs key on `github.run_id`.
rationale: Release and main/dev CI runs are observed by downstream `workflow_run` triggers, which must see them complete rather than cancelled. Reasons moved out of `.github/workflows/ci.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The template slop-scan config exempts test files from `tests.duplicate-mock-setup` only
description: `.bkit/templates/slop-scan.config.json` scopes its test-file override to `tests.duplicate-mock-setup`; type-escape casts and duplicate signatures in tests are findings like anywhere else, and `slop:delta` fails only on new ones. The shipped `guardrails.cjs` hooks carry a per-file opt-out.
rationale: `.agents/rules.md` "fix code, not gates": exemptions are per file with a reason, never a whole category. bkit's own config already ran this way.

summary: bkit's own graphify rollup uses `MMD_MIN_WEIGHT=6`
rationale: At 6 the capabilities diagram draws 21 files and 32 links; 12 drops it to 11 files. Reason moved out of the script comment (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit carries no code, flag, command or setting without a production caller
description: Removed 2026-10-10: named managed blocks and the `optional` block flag (`extractNamedBlocks`); the `bkit codex` verb (no handler); `--keep-npmrc`; `bkit prs guard-checkout`; `bkit branches rebase --onto/--abort`; `bkit runs dispatch --retrigger-suffix` and its `autoroute-mismatch` result; the telemetry archive (`writeRollupShard`, `foldWithArchive`, `archiveShardPaths`); the install staging dir helpers; `validateInvariants`; `parseStatus`; `PROGRAM_GATEWAYS`; `HARVEST_TIMEOUT_MS`; `ADDITIVE_LABELS`; the `package.json` keys `bkit.renovateRunner` and `bkit.depUpdater: "renovate"`; tests that only asserted removed flags are rejected. Test helpers live in test files.
rationale: Owner 2026-10-10: "do not keep unused features, remove all". Evidence per item: no importer outside its own test, no call site in workflows/prompts/CI/hooks, or no caller passing the option.

summary: bkit's own pnpm overrides and allowed build scripts live in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`
rationale: pnpm 11 ignores `pnpm.overrides` in `package.json` and blocks esbuild's build script unless allowed. Reason moved out of config comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's own renovate.json5 holds vite and pnpm major updates
rationale: pnpm 11 ignores `pnpm.overrides` in `package.json` (they move to `pnpm-workspace.yaml`) and blocks esbuild's build script unless it is listed in `onlyBuiltDependencies`, so a pnpm major would drop the vite pin. Reason moved out of the renovate.json5 comment (owner rule 2026-10-10).
description: `.github/renovate.json5` (bkit repo only) disables major updates for vite and pnpm; minor and patch stay enabled. vite stays on ^6 through `pnpm.overrides` in `package.json`.

summary: All 11 #467 section 4 centralisation items, the four outside-workflow items and the three excluded hook items are built, after #507's file move
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Items: steps finish, {BKIT} placeholder, land-on-dev helpers, workflows fail/handover, fids find/workflows promote, workflows close --outbox/links, labels into runs dispatch, ship-only helpers, auto runs context, steps gate in every gate, parseFlags placeholder guard; bkit ci prose, steps stub, one cloud context job, husky skip-CI regex from SKIP_CI_TOKEN; shared preflight.sh, slimmer cloud-bootstrap.sh, one gateguard/guardrails source. Done after the move so new commands land in their final folders.

summary: The package splits `.bkit/templates/` into `.bkit/core/` (PolyForm, written and kept current), `.bkit/shared/` (MIT-0, written and kept current) and `.bkit/templates/` (MIT-0, copy-and-own); a file's path inside its folder is where it lands
rationale: Reverses the #489 decision of 2026-10-09 to copy only the template set and leave the package layout alone. That decision weighed the split against the cost of moving install paths and had no licence reason; #506 licenses bkit as PolyForm with low-IP files under MIT-0, and a licence must say which files are which without reading `isTemplate`.

summary: The engine lives at `.bkit/core/engine/`, split into `commands/` (what you type) and `install/`, `render/`, `checks/before/`, `checks/after/`, `ledgers/`, `shared/`, `tools/`; no `bkit-` prefix inside; tests sit next to the file they test, and tests that read shipped text sit in `audits/`
rationale: Owner 2026-10-10 approved the layout and file names posted on #507 (comment 6094807529), including its renames table. `engine/` not `src/` because every other path in `core/` is where install writes the file; `checks/before` and `checks/after` because detection runs before and after writing, and `preflight`/`postinstall` read as npm lifecycle hooks; `bin` points at `dist/cli.js`.

summary: No bkit release until #507's folder split lands; the pre-release check fails when `.bkit/templates/` holds anything but copy-and-own templates
rationale: `.bkit/templates/LICENSE.md` (MIT-0, c3fe30a8) covers that folder, which still holds `AGENTS.md`, the plan and audit templates and other core files until the split moves them; a release in between would put them under MIT-0.

summary: Ship's close and flush helpers live in `commands/workflow/workflows.ts`
rationale: Putting them in `branches.ts` makes `branches.ts` and `workflows.ts` import each other.

summary: The Failure Path passes its error text to `workflows fail` / `issues comment` through `--error-file`, not a heredoc
rationale: Quotes or backticks in an error message broke the heredoc; a file carries any text unchanged.

summary: Every workflow re-asks the agent when its verdict header is PENDING (exit 5) or invalid (exit 6)
rationale: Build, debug and ship sent these to the Failure Path while design and plan re-asked; one rule, and a fixable agent slip no longer ends the run.

summary: The clamp-log helpers live in `ledgers/clamp-log.ts`
rationale: A file in `commands/workflow/` must be a command, and keeping the helpers out of `context.ts` broke an import cycle that crashed whenever `steps.ts` loaded first.

summary: The code all hosts' hooks share lives in `.bkit/core/hooks/` (moved there as `core/hook-parts/`, then renamed by #507), outside the templates folder
rationale: Under `.bkit/templates/` the install walk copied it to a `hook-parts/` folder at the root of the user's repo; it is bkit-written source spliced in at render time (`render/parts.ts`), not a template.

summary: Workflows run `bkit comply` before `workflows close`
description: Superseded by `467-compliance-graded-inside-workflows-close`: `bkit workflows close` grades compliance itself before writing its report, and no workflow calls `bkit comply`.
rationale: The close comment showed the grade of the previous run when comply ran after it.

summary: A file bkit stops shipping is deleted only when unchanged since bkit wrote it; an edited copy is kept with an advisory, callers are reported, and no shim is left at the old path
description: Superseded by `489-no-migration-code`: bkit carries no upgrade, migration or legacy-compat code. The retire engine (bkit-retire) was deleted in 8badea26; canonicalHashes now serve only the upgrade/uninstall drift checks, and a stale entry for an absent path is pruned by the install/upgrade merge (mergeCanonicalHashes).
rationale: Install and upgrade overwrite what bkit owns but never delete a file bkit has dropped, so a retired script would otherwise sit in every consumer repo forever; a consumer-edited copy stays; caller lines get their own advisory because nothing else tells the consumer the call now fails. Why no forwarding shim is left at a retired path is not written down.

summary: Auto's CI mode reads the PR body through `gh`; there is no tracker MCP fallback
rationale: The CI-run lookup in the same step already needs `gh`; a second path for one field is not worth keeping.

summary: Workflows derive the auto-route suffix from `bkit issues labels` on the labels already read through MCP
rationale: The `gh issue view` reads broke the tracker-reads-through-MCP rule and failed silently on Linear or without `gh`. Linear issues now get the marker too.

summary: Auto's Timeouts line is 3600s, like the other workflows
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Auto hands off to a phase workflow that runs under 3600s; one value lets the line be one shared clause.

summary: Branch sync merges ledger conflicts by union, aborts on a conflict outside `docs/`, and treats a failed fetch as fatal
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Ledgers are append-only, so union loses no rows where taking dev's side dropped the branch's rows; a code conflict needs a person or the conflict-resolve agent; syncing against a stale dev hides real conflicts.

summary: Build commits its test-run log, clamped, under `docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/`
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. In `.git/bkit-outbox` only, it was lost with the worktree.

summary: Cleanup removes only marked worktrees; a branch held by an unmarked worktree keeps both its local and remote branch, and cleanup names the worktree
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. The local delete failed silently while the remote branch was still deleted.

summary: Design and plan worktrees install dependencies like build and debug
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Without an install there is no `.husky/_`, so commits and pushes in those worktrees skipped the hooks, and the design-spike subagent had no `node_modules`.

summary: Design Step 3 skips a related issue whose comments don't parse and names it in the design inputs
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Related issues are background; one bad comment should not stop a design.

summary: A required flag given an empty value exits 2 (USAGE)
rationale: An empty `--head=` from a failed probe went into the ship re-validate loop and a 170-minute mirror poll.

summary: Every workflow runs the strict FID check at Step 1, with or without a tracker; `prs open` keeps its check as a backstop
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. A bad FID failed only at `prs open`, after the work was done; design with no tracker skipped the Step 1 check.

summary: A failed dependency install stops build, debug and ship
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Ship runs tests and the merge check; carrying on without dependencies only fails later with a less clear error.

summary: The pre-worktree commit passes the repo root explicitly
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Without it the commit runs wherever the shell is, which can be a subfolder or another checkout.

summary: `bkit branches rebase` aborts a refused rebase itself, before writing its log and sentinel
rationale: Leaving it in progress made the abort depend on the Failure Path running `workflows fail`. The abort resets tracked files, so it runs before the log and sentinel are written.

summary: Runtime detection has no `REPO_ROOT`/`FID` env fallback, and there is no `BKIT_MIRROR_GATE_SH` hook
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Workflows pass flags; the mirror-gate variable was test-only (489-no-code-without-a-production-caller).

summary: Ship's post-merge check passes or fails on the `bkit-tests-check` capstone job alone
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. The capstone is the job branch protection requires and it decides what counts; other jobs (deploys, notifications) cannot fail the close of an already-merged PR.

summary: Ship's skill prune warns and carries on: a missing `.agents/skills.md` skips the prune, a failed uninstall is reported
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. The PR has merged by then and pruning is housekeeping; a missing registry must never uninstall every skill.

summary: A stale lock is reclaimed as soon as its holder is idle; the lock file's age is not checked
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Reverts the 30-minute file-age condition. No further reason is written down.

summary: Status rows use `verdict` for complexity, `timeout_s` for ship, always write `attempt`, and record the PR URL in `artifacts`
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Reverts the #467 renames (`complexity`, `timeoutS`, `attempt` omitted at 0, `prUrl`). No further reason is written down.

summary: `steps done` refuses a PASS with failures, a FAIL without, and missing or empty artifacts; debug diagnose requires `Mode:`
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. A contradictory row means the subagent output is wrong; catching it at write time is cheaper than acting on a bad verdict later. Debug routes on `Mode:`.

summary: `bkit steps gate` checks a row's `strategy`, `scope` and `attempt` wherever the step writes them
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. The checklist lines were dropped while `steps done` still wrote the fields, so a row missing one passed its gate. The check lives in code, not in lines the agent ticks.

summary: A step's allowed verdict values and header fields are declared once, in its prompt; workflow gates no longer repeat them
rationale: `steps finish` reads the prompt's declaration, so a value list in the workflow could only drift from it.

summary: The wording check covers the workflows and the audit templates; per-family clauses and block-position checks are not built
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. 92 sentences repeat across the workflows and 83 across the audit templates with no check, and the workflow header lines had drifted.

summary: The wording check splits sentences on `;`, requires `No commits` only in prompts that list `Bash`, and checks the whole header order
rationale: The `;` split and the Bash condition were agreed with the 2026-09-25 measurement and not built. The check missed a drifted fifth copy, a drifted Mandate line and swapped header lines.

summary: NEVER = forbidden everywhere; do not = forbidden in this step; mixed-case do NOT retired
description: Two distinct forms replace the interchangeable `NEVER` / `do NOT` mix. `NEVER` marks a hard limit forbidden everywhere, at all times; lowercase `do not` marks a prohibition scoped to the step. `do NOT` is retired — it added emphasis without marking a tier.
rationale: No prompt guide read distinguishes `NEVER` from `do NOT`; OpenAI groups `NEVER` with the invariant markers, Anthropic prefers the positive form. The audit counted 393 `do NOT` and 183 `NEVER` across the prompts, 16 lines carrying both, with no recorded difference.
alternatives: Drop `NEVER` for `do not` everywhere — rejected: a hard limit forbidden at all times is worth marking distinctly, and OpenAI guide backs it.

summary: One short reason clause allowed on a hard limit a model would otherwise misread
description: `.bkit/prompts.md` § Prompt Authoring Rules § Dense instructions only keeps no-rationale as the default and carves one exception: a single short reason clause on a hard limit whose boundary a model would otherwise misread or over-apply. The exception reaches prompts and workflows through § Notation.
rationale: Anthropic guide asks for the reason behind an instruction and no prompt guide read forbids it; the blanket ban departed from it. A one-clause reason costs ~5-15 tokens and only where the boundary is non-obvious. bkit-ship-conflict-resolve already carried the one recorded example.
alternatives: Keep the blanket ban — rejected: no guide read supports it and Anthropic asks for the reason. Allow a reason on every rule — rejected: every byte is paid on every run.

summary: Capitals mark only a hard limit; closed list NEVER, ALWAYS, MUST, ONLY, PROHIBITED
description: Notation rule (`.bkit/prompts.md` § Notation; binds prompts, workflows, `.agents/rules.md` and docs): a word takes capitals only when it marks a hard limit — a destructive, irreversible or security-sensitive action, or a required field / machine-parsed invariant. Closed list `NEVER`, `ALWAYS`, `MUST`, `ONLY`, `PROHIBITED`; everything else lowercase, scope quantifiers and joining words included. One capitalised word per clause; never inside a label, a parenthetical or a description.
rationale: OpenAI GPT-5.6 reserves ALWAYS / NEVER / must / only for true invariants; Anthropic says dial back aggressive wording on current models; no prompt guide read supports capitals on judgement calls. The 2026-10 prompt audit (prompts-3, HIGH) found ~60% of bkit 1,021 capitalised prompt words on process / judgement lines, and the style predates every current model pin.
alternatives: Capitalise scope quantifiers (ALL / ANY / EVERY) as invariants — rejected: they mark scope, not safety or a required field, and no guide supports them. Keep the mixed-case NOT contrast marker — rejected: emphasis without a tier.

summary: Summary output cap applies to prose only; sections listing items verbatim are exempt
description: Shared `output-cap` wording clause (`.bkit/wording.md` § output-cap; reaches the four summary prompts and bkit-debug-abort-handover): apply max 500 token limit to **Create** prose; sections that list items verbatim are exempt. Cap-table row in `.bkit/prompts.md` restated to match.
rationale: The 2026-10 prompt audit (prompts-5) found the blanket 500-token cap always lost to the verbatim-list clause — 35 of 36 sampled summary outputs over cap, median 1,686 words. The cap exists for Linear comment readability; the verbatim lists are the human's decision surface where rewording loses the trade-off. Scoping preserves both instead of sacrificing either.
alternatives: Drop the cap — rejected: loses the Linear UX guard the cap exists for. Cut the verbatim requirement — rejected: a reworded acceptance item or option loses the trade-off the human decides on. Raise the cap — rejected: no data picks a new number.

summary: Plan split decision keys on task count (<= 12); unestimable 85K token figure dropped
description: `bkit-plan-complexity-check` verdict maps `SINGLE` = task count <= 12, `SPLIT` = task count > 12; `bkit-plan-complexity-split` sizes sub-plans at <= 12 tasks (ceil(tasks / 12) sub-plans). The 85K estimated-token threshold and the estimation step removed from both prompts.
rationale: The 2026-10 prompt audit (prompts-11) found the split decision rested on an estimated-token figure with no estimation method — a number no agent can derive. Task count is countable by grep, was already the secondary anchor, and gates / domain areas remain counted as advisory context. Adding invented gate or domain thresholds would repeat the same ungrounded-number problem.
alternatives: Define a token-estimation method — rejected: any per-task token constant would be as ungrounded as 85K. Add gate / domain thresholds — rejected: no data picks the numbers.

summary: No CI gate on open CRITICAL failures and no automated stale-deferral report; the failures and deferrals audits cover both on cadence
description: #346 proposed gating CI on open CRITICAL failures and reporting stale OPEN deferrals. Decision: not built. docs/templates/bkit-audit-failures.md and docs/templates/bkit-audit-deferrals.md already encode the required semantics (open = status != CLOSED incl. TRIAGED; age from the earliest row per key; case-insensitive severity; ts/status data-defect checks) on a per-cycle / monthly cadence, with an extra pass on new CRITICAL rows. The failures audit gate question (bkit-audit-failures.md:52, :106) recording the gate as absent is the decided state, not a gap. Two incidental fixes stay open: ledger-integrity.test.ts validates envelope/kind/reason/future-ts but not severity, status or ts:0 (bad rows: failure severity "low" duplicated; deferral 384-mode-3-bookkeeping-e2e-deferred-to-341-live-run ts:0); .bkit/jsonl.md:145 (CRITICAL triage before next release) contradicts :254 (TRIAGED is STILL open WORK).
rationale: The proposal risk (open CRITICALs invisible, stale deferrals forgotten) is already mitigated by the audit cadence that landed after #80 closed; a second continuous mechanism duplicates it and would contradict the schema (jsonl.md:145 vs :254). 0 open CRITICAL failures and 68 open deferrals (none HIGH or CRITICAL) mean a gate would never fire today.
alternatives: Build the gate inside bkit check, failing on release only (release.yml would need a new step) - rejected (owner, 2026-10-11): the audits are enough.

summary: plan grounded on the canonical design despite no Parent design marker
description: Issue #504 carried no **Parent design:** marker, so /bkit-plan Step 1 would default PARENT_FID empty (standalone plan). The canonical design docs/plans/202610/504-example-project-design.md exists for the same FID and month and the issue is design-driven, so it was treated as the parent design and appended to plan-input-1.md.
rationale: A plan cannot be generated faithfully without its design; producing a standalone plan over an existing canonical design would be an incomplete shortcut.
alternatives: literal standalone plan on issue input alone (PARENT_FID empty)

summary: bkit ships no auto-compaction threshold; earlier compaction is a consumer setting, documented per host in `.bkit/providers.md` § Context compaction and offered as a setup tip (#543)
description: Claude Code: `autoCompactWindow` in `.claude/settings.json` (install keeps consumer keys). Codex: `model_auto_compact_token_limit` above the first `[table]` in `.codex/config.toml`. opencode: no absolute trigger, per-model `limit.input` workaround only. Cursor and Antigravity: no setting. A live Claude Code 2.1.299 run confirmed subagents (built-in general-purpose and custom) auto-compact under a project `autoCompactWindow`; Codex 0.162.1 source copies the parent config into spawned agents.
rationale: Earlier compaction trades summary detail and agent-kill risk (`Autocompact is thrashing`) against re-read cost, and 300k has not been quality-checked on a real build. That trade-off is the consumer's to make. Shipped in `.bkit/shared/.claude/settings.json` it could not be changed in the committed file, because install restores template keys.
alternatives: Ship `autoCompactWindow: 300000` and a bkit-managed `.codex/config.toml` block (implemented, then withdrawn: enforces an untested trade-off on every consumer); seed per-model opencode limits (needs model-window tracking, side effects untested).

summary: Claude Code on the web no longer gets `CLAUDE_AUTOCOMPACT_PCT_OVERRIDE=70` from bkit's cloud setup
description: Removed the constant from `.bkit/core/engine/install/cloud-env.ts` (and the now-unused `constants` field of `CloudEnvPolicy`), from the cloud advisory and from `.bkit/cloud.md`. `.bkit/cloud.md` points to `autoCompactWindow` in committed `.claude/settings.json`, which applies to cloud sessions as-is.
rationale: Compaction is a consumer choice (`549-compaction-threshold-is-a-tip-not-shipped`); a bkit-pinned env constant made that choice for every cloud session. One consumer-owned setting in committed settings covers local and cloud alike, and a percentage would compound with it.
alternatives: Keep the constant as the cloud-only default.

summary: Shipped rule: prefer context-fetch blocks or the provider's CLI over MCP for logs, errors and database reads
description: One guidance line in `.agents/rules.md` § Testing & Debugging (`Provider data`), worded as a preference so consumers who wired an MCP server on purpose are not broken.
rationale: Every connected MCP tool costs tokens on every request even when unused; in the measured consumer repo, provider connectors (Supabase, Sentry, Vercel) were the bulk of the starting load and their uses are covered by context-fetch blocks and CLIs. Turning connectors off and locking MCP URLs to one project are setup tips (#543), not rules.
alternatives: Ship `disableClaudeAiConnectors` as a default; rename `.agents/context.md` to `tools.md` with CLI recipes replacing MCP servers (dropped: deferred loading makes MCP cost mostly tool names, most of them from claude.ai connectors).

summary: bkit carries no upgrade, migration or legacy-compat code
rationale: Owner 2026-10-10: "we do NOT have to worry about existing users upgrading migrating - there are only two and we control both so any migration considerations are dead code as well". The two installs are this repo and consumer-a; old paths there are fixed by hand after a release. Superseded 2026-10-14 by `public-installs-get-upgrade-migrations`: bkit is published publicly on npmjs, so installs bkit does not control exist.
description: Removed: retire lists (bkit-retire.ts), package.json repoint (bkit-package-json.ts), config.md to context.md migration (bkit-context-migrate.ts), telemetry migrate/validate/normalise, tier3Hashes fold, pre-envelope and envelope readers, hash-comment marker style, opencode provider aliases, status.json rewrite and fallback, legacy advisories.

summary: Agents never add migration code unasked; they suggest it with what breaks without it and build it only on explicit confirmation, registering it in docs/migrations.md
rationale: Owner 2026-10-10: a project rule not to add migration code unasked, only suggest. Shims added with each format change were never removed and accumulated (about 10,900 lines removed in #489).

summary: `bkit upgrade` alone carries an existing install forward wherever a changed format, path or flag would otherwise leave it broken or insecure; every migration is registered in docs/migrations.md
rationale: Owner 2026-10-14: bkit is public, so installs exist that the owner cannot fix by hand after a release. First case: the OpenCode network allows bkit 5.1.0 and earlier wrote as `*{host}*` auto-allow attacker URLs, and OpenCode's last-match-wins kept them winning over the anchored replacements on every upgrade. A register keeps each migration visible so it can be retired once no supported install predates it.

summary: rules.md Universal Rules: `Language server first` and `Narrow text search first` for search, `Code reads` and `Command output` for reading; a one-line `**Code reads:**` header clause in every prompt
rationale: Owner 2026-10-14 (#550): 456 transcripts from a bkit user repo put Bash output at 29.8% of cost, about 60% of it sed / grep / cat reading source, and 41% of file reads repeated a file the same agent had already read. Lossy compression corrupted code in the #545 replay, so reading less is the fix. Most measured runs were ad-hoc general-purpose agents that only rules.md reaches; the header clause keeps the rule in front of bkit agents. Serena was configured but almost unused (40 results vs 9,848 sed reads), so symbol lookup is ordered first rather than offered alongside text search; it stays conditional (when configured) because Serena ships as a template only.
alternatives: Lossy compression of tool output (rejected: corrupted code and elided function bodies in the #545 replay); a Serena-only rule (rejected: Serena is optional).

summary: /bkit-design Step 3 Grill: the orchestrator interviews the human in rounds (default on, `grill=false` skips, 10-round cap), writes design-grill-{RUN}.md and appends it to design-input-{RUN}.md; design-generate reads design-input; design is removed from bkit-cloud.yml workflow_dispatch
rationale: Owner 2026-10-14 (#548): kick design off with an interview so the design rests on the human's decisions, not the issue text alone. Inside the workflow, not a separate skill: design never starts unattended (bkit-cloud.yml auto-routes only to ship / debug), so the only unattended entry was the manual dispatch choice, now removed. Runs in the orchestrator because subagents cannot reach the human. Plain-text rounds, not AskUserQuestion, because that tool caps at 4 questions x 4 options and is Claude-only. Unanswered questions at the cap are recorded `Assumed, not confirmed` so designers can tell a human decision from an agent guess. The section is `Settled`, not `Decisions`, because design-generate writes its own `Decisions` section. Appending to design-input reaches every input reader with no per-agent read-list change; design-generate gains design-input because it previously read only the brainstorms, so a decision reached it only if the ideate agents carried it through. Waiting time is exempt from the 3600s timeout; the 30-minute lock-idle reclaim is accepted because only the person being grilled runs design for that issue. The cap is a literal, not a `MAX_*` threshold, because rounds are not recorded in status.jsonl. Method adapted from Matt Pocock's `grilling` skill (MIT), written in bkit's own words with credit in .bkit/workflows.md only, since workflow files carry no commentary or external links.
alternatives: A separate pre-design skill that posts decisions as an issue comment (rejected by owner: grill belongs at the start of design itself); vendoring grill-me / grilling verbatim (rejected: bkit writes its own wording); grilling at bkit-plan (rejected: by plan time decisions are in the design); a counted MAX_GRILL_ROUNDS threshold (rejected: nothing records rounds).

summary: ReadGuard: advisory repeat-read hook on all five hosts, file reads only, log per (session, agent), cleared for the whole session on compaction
rationale: Owner 2026-10-14 (#550): 41% of measured file reads repeated a read by the same agent. Advisory only, never blocks. All five hosts for provider parity, with host gaps documented (Codex shell only; no subagent id on Codex / Cursor / Antigravity; no compaction signal on Antigravity and opencode 2.0; opencode delivers after the read). Repeated fetch commands are left to the rules.md Command output rule: an identical-command check would flag legitimate CI polling. Compaction clears every agent of the session because hosts do not say whether a subagent compacted; clearing too much only drops notes, never adds a wrong one. The note always tells the agent to re-read when the earlier output is no longer in its context, covering the gaps.
alternatives: Claude Code first, other hosts later (rejected: provider parity rule). A list of read-only fetch commands to watch (rejected: polling noise). Blocking repeat reads (rejected: an agent whose context was summarised needs the re-read).

summary: On Antigravity, hook advisories (GateGuard checklist, ReadGuard note, guardrails fetch / shell-edit advisories) deny the call once with the advisory as the reason; the identical retry is allowed
rationale: Owner 2026-10-14 (#550), after a live agy probe: only a deny reason reaches the model; an allow reason is dropped, and a PreInvocation injectSteps hook disables every hook in hooks.json. One blocked call is the only way the agent sees the advisory.
alternatives: Read the real input but keep replying allow (rejected: advisories never reach the model on Antigravity). PreInvocation ephemeralMessage injection (rejected: a PreInvocation entry stops all hooks firing).

summary: #363 — the dev stale-run guard compares CI-run recency, never the git tip
description: The guard queries the most recently COMPLETED dev CI run (gh run list --branch dev --workflow bkit-ci.yml --status completed) and compares its headSha against the triggering workflow_run head SHA. An empty run list fails OPEN and dispatches.
rationale: ship pushes its terminal close commit to dev WHILE the post-merge CI run is still going, so a git rev-parse origin/dev comparison mismatches on every legitimate dispatch and silently suppresses the whole feature. Close commits carry [skip ci], so they never trigger CI and never become the most-recent-completed head — which makes that head the intended staleness signal. Fail-open beats swallowing the feature on a transient API hiccup.
alternatives: compare against the git tip (git rev-parse origin/dev) — suppresses every legitimate dispatch; fail closed on an empty run list — trades a transient API error for a dropped feature

summary: Consumer-shipped docs describe the current setup only — no tracker issue numbers, ledger keys, or project history
description: Every manifest-listed .md plus the docs/ payload templates and their canonical seeds carry no internal identifier (tracker issue number, ledger key such as the retired KN-N / DE-N scheme, coined review-finding or guard name) and no project history. Decisions live in docs/decisions.jsonl, incidents in docs/knowledge.jsonl — ledgers whose rows carry those references as data. Each doc states the constraint in its own Rules block; bkit-shipped-docs-refs.test.ts enforces it over the manifest corpus, skipping fenced blocks so placeholders and anchors do not false-trip.
rationale: an internal id means nothing in a consumer repo and ages into a wrong claim as soon as the referenced work moves. The prior rule pushed labels OUT of .bkit/core/workflows/*.md and INTO .bkit/workflows.md, which itself ships — so the labels never actually left the consumer surface. 61 sites across 10 docs had accumulated.
alternatives: keep .bkit/workflows.md as the sanctioned label home (it ships, so this only moves the problem); allow refs but date-stamp them (still meaningless to a consumer); strip refs by convention with no guard test (this is the third sweep of the same class)

summary: workflow step width is decided by input presence per lens, never by a size scalar
description: Each skippable lens step in bkit-design and bkit-plan carries a machine-checkable predicate over an artifact an earlier step produced — zero declared dependency edges, no [MODIFY]/[DELETE] rows, Required Capabilities = None, Failures = 0, MILESTONE absent from the labels. A consumer glob list (package.json bkit.sensitivePaths, default []) may force a lens ON; it may never drop one. bkit-build, bkit-debug and bkit-ship get no step changes.
rationale: A NARROW|STANDARD|WIDE scalar collapses several independent facts into one number and then lets arbitrary filename numbering pick the survivor: on plan Step 5, NARROW=run-1 keeps the tightness lens (the one most duplicated by Step 7's scope check) and drops both dependency correctness and regression risk. The parallel siblings are not redundant copies — each carries an explicit Lens: line — so cutting width by count silently deletes a dimension. A lens whose input is absent reads, finds no instances and returns PASS having looked at nothing; that absence is machine-checkable and is a far better justification than a size feeling.
alternatives: NARROW|STANDARD|WIDE scale dial keyed on issue size; a per-run caller flag choosing width; keeping full width everywhere (the status quo, which is what drives people to route around the pipeline)

summary: plan escalates to design automatically, with no human approval gate; default entry for all non-reproducing work is /bkit-plan
description: After Generate Plan and before the Step 5 review fan-out, plan reads an Escalate: TRUE|FALSE verdict. TRUE stops the run, records the verdict, and hands to /bkit-design. Design is entered only by escalation from plan. Debug keeps its own failure-driven entry, and a bug with no failing test routes to plan rather than closing debug green.
rationale: An orchestrator with free choice of steps drifts toward the cheap path, and a skipped step leaves no artifact, so the drift is invisible — but that only bites on downgrades. Escalation is the expensive direction, and an agent choosing 'this needs a design phase' is never the lazy choice. With build's plan requirement intact there is nothing below plan to downgrade into, so the only automatic move available is upward and needs no human standing in for it. Cost when the entry guess is wrong is one wasted plan-generate run, because the verdict lands before the review fan-out.
alternatives: a human approval gate on every escalation (blocks the one direction that cannot be abused); design-by-default entry (the status quo, which pays a full design phase on every bug fix); a comment-only plan or a direct-to-build route (rejected outright — build's existing plan-file requirement is the floor and does not move)

summary: Claude sessions stay in acceptEdits with workspace trust granted host-side and no ask row on shell curl/wget — the only combination that reaches zero permission prompts without putting a classifier in the loop
description: Three levers decide how often a Claude session stops to ask, and only one combination reaches zero. (1) defaultMode stays acceptEdits: it is the one value of the three that actually takes effect from .claude/settings.json, and it leaves the blanket Bash(*) allow in force. (2) Workspace trust is granted host-side by the generated cloud setup script, without which every allow row is ignored and each Bash call prompts. (3) Shell curl and wget carry no ask row, because a content-scoped ask is evaluated before the auto-mode classifier and always forces a prompt that a cloud session cannot answer. Destructive-git and .env-read ask rows are deliberately kept: every destructive-git command is already on the PROHIBITED list in all five workflow headers, so none fires in normal operation and they cost no friction.
rationale: The goal is the fewest interruptions per workflow run, with mistakes absorbed by git rather than by prompts. acceptEdits plus trust plus no network ask row produces no prompts and no classifier round-trip on any command. The kept rows guard the one class git cannot undo: untracked files and uncommitted work have no reflog, so git clean -fd and git checkout -- . are unrecoverable in a way a bad commit never is. Claude cannot express a per-domain curl allow at all — its rules match a command prefix, not a URL host — so blanket-allow was the only alternative to a prompt on every fetch.
alternatives: Switch defaultMode to auto — REJECTED, and it does not work where it would be set: auto has no effect from .claude/settings.json or .claude/settings.local.json (it also suppresses a user-scope defaultMode), and even applied from user settings it is higher friction, not lower, because auto mode drops blanket Bash(*) and routes every shell command through the classifier, adding a round-trip per command, classifier blocks as a new failure mode, and a fallback to prompting after three consecutive blocks. Keep the curl/wget ask rows and ratify them into the parity suite — REJECTED: one guaranteed prompt per context=web context-fetch block, unanswerable in cloud. Port Cursor's URL-host-parsing guardrail to Claude and opencode — the correct fix for the remaining edge (an undeclared host is ungated on Claude) but a materially larger build; left open on 441.

summary: BAR-142 §A5 — `bkit upgrade` diff engine + `canonicalHashes`
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** (1) `canonicalHashes` is an additive field in `.bkit/version` (v0.9.x+): map of consumer-relative path → sha256 of bkit-written content at install time. (2) `bkit upgrade` uses `isConsumerModified(relPath, absPath, canonicalHashes)` to detect consumer drift: if disk hash ≠ canonical hash → conflict, do NOT overwrite. (3) `--non-interactive`: auto-apply non-conflicting; emit conflict list to stderr; exit non-zero on any conflict. (4) `updateCanonicalHashesAfterUpgrade` updates hashes for upgraded files post-run.
- **Why:** Silent overwrite of consumer drift was the root cause of the consumer-a regression (KN-8). `canonicalHashes` gives the upgrade engine a per-file ownership record that survives across installs. Backward-compat: absent field → `{}` → all files appear "unknown" → conservative no-overwrite (safe).
- **Discarded:** (1) Three-way merge UI — OOS per plan. (2) Timestamp-based drift detection — unreliable across CI environments (git checkout resets mtime). (3) Storing full file content in `.bkit-version` — too large; sha256 is sufficient for drift detection.
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-142 §A5, `.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/upgrade.ts`, `.bkit/core/engine/install/version-file.ts`, `.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/upgrade.test.ts`, `.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/upgrade.integration.test.ts`, KN-8
rationale: Silent overwrite of consumer drift was the root cause of the consumer-a regression (KN-8). `canonicalHashes` gives the upgrade engine a per-file ownership record that survives across installs. Backward-compat: absent field → `{}` → all files appear "unknown" → conservative no-overwrite (safe).

summary: BAR-167 — Drop `__bkit__` envelope; adopt deep-containment ownership model
rationale: The `__bkit__` envelope caused two real-world failure modes on 2026-05-09 consumer audit: (1) duplicate content — the same hook block appeared inside `__bkit__` AND at the top level, causing confusion and bloat; (2) silent drift — `.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` lost its `pnpm bkit check` step with no detection. The envelope model required consumers to hold two copies of every bkit-owned key. Deep-containment eliminates the duplication: the template IS the declared scope; the consumer only needs to contain it. Consumer-added keys outside the template tree are never touched. `writeTier2Json` THROW (envelope guard) was a footgun — deep-containment removes the need for it entirely.

summary: .bkit/issues.jsonl replaces docs/completed.md as the sole shipped-feature record
description: Design Addendum 2 § H (owner, 2026-07-25): docs/completed.md is DELETED, not dual-written. `.bkit/issues.jsonl` (`kind:"feature"`) is the sole shipped-feature record. There is no migration command: `bkit telemetry migrate` (`.md`->`.jsonl` pairs, bootstrap seed) was removed with the other migration code (8badea26).
rationale: Two records of one shipped-feature fact drift; the ship verdict grep and the board fold both read the single ledger.
alternatives: Dual-write (retain completed.md as a generated human view) — REJECTED: nobody reads the .md (humans read roadmap.md; the sole machine reader is the ship verdict grep), so it is pure drift risk with no consumer.

summary: BAR-148 — post-CI routing runs `/bkit-auto` from `bkit-cloud.yml`; `claude-code-action@v1` is still the Claude dispatch surface
description: The `bkit-ci-router` orchestrator, its GHA workflow, its template and `runCiRouterModule` are deleted. `.github/workflows/bkit-cloud.yml` dispatches `/bkit-auto <phase> <arg>` via `anthropics/claude-code-action@v1`; a second `opencode` dispatch job runs beside it.
rationale: Self-contained, no webhook bridge, no claude.ai dependency. Consumer needs only one new secret + one workflow file. Anthropic actively maintains the action — survives runtime / model changes. consumer-a's `ci-complete.yml` already proved the surrounding scaffold (PR lookup, branch filter, Linear comment-back); only the dispatch step changes.

summary: BAR-148 — post-CI routing stays a separate fresh session, not a step inside `/bkit-build`
description: The router is `/bkit-auto`, dispatched by `.github/workflows/bkit-cloud.yml` in its own session after CI completes. `/bkit-build` itself now has 18 steps (Step 17 Summary, Step 18 Close Workflow & Create PR), so the original 'closes at Step 17' / 'Step 18 discarded' wording no longer applies; what holds is that routing is not a step of the build. Handoff state is the per-FID `status.jsonl`; the shared contract doc is `.bkit/workflows.md`.
rationale: Chaining `bkit-ship` (~12 steps) or `bkit-debug` (loop bounded by `MAX_DEBUG_ATTEMPT`) into the same orchestrator session compounds context-window pressure: cumulative `COMMENT_BODY` per step, repeated `status.json` re-reads, gate verifications quoting earlier SHAs / PR numbers verbatim. Fresh-session split keeps every orchestrator's context bounded; downstream skills already implement Resume from `status.json`.

summary: #168 — design and plan summaries carry Outstanding Questions verbatim; every summary ends with an advisory Recommended Next Step
description: `bkit-design-summary.md` and `bkit-plan-summary.md` both carry `## Outstanding Questions`, copied verbatim from the artifact (options, `Recommended`, `Default if unanswered`) — the summary agent does not generate its own recommendation. Empty state is `None`. All five summaries carry `## Recommended Next Step`, advisory only, never auto-triggered. There is no dedicated tracker comment: both sections ship inside the one `Step N — Summary` comment.
rationale: A reworded option loses the trade-off the human is deciding on, so questions are copied, not paraphrased. One summary comment keeps the handoff in one place.

references: .bkit/core/workflows/bkit-debug.md` (Steps renumbered 1-10; Step 3 Run-Tests routing incl. NORMAL-exhaustion → SOAK; Step 5 diagnose `Mode: SOAK` budget reset; Step 7 soak `SOAK_ATTEMPT`; Step 10 no-leak assertion)
summary: #143 — OBSERVE mode removed; observation logging folds into SOAK; NORMAL-exhaustion → SOAK on a fresh budget
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** OBSERVE is removed from `/bkit-debug` entirely — DE-24's `NORMAL|OBSERVE|SOAK` ladder becomes **`NORMAL|SOAK`**. OBSERVE was gated solely on `DEBUG_ATTEMPT == 2` (a weak proxy: debug re-runs for many unrelated reasons — CI flakes, the ci-router re-routing a fresh failure, manual re-runs), instrumented **before** diagnosis (old Step 3 ran ahead of the Step-6 diagnose, so its instrument points were blind), and its evidence capture was structurally brittle — the orchestrator's only marker-capturing re-run (Fetch Context's local-test sub-fetch) is unit-scope, so `[DEBUG-OBSERVE]` lines fired in an out-of-process / live-stack process (the runtime-only bug class #143 exists for) were never recorded. SOAK already owns the instrument-with-`[DEBUG-OBSERVE]` → observe → strip cycle (its prompt Process step 4), run by an agent that controls its own loop and is not bound by the orchestrator's fixed capture — so OBSERVE was a strict subset of SOAK via the worse mechanism. Changes: (1) delete Step 3 (Observe Instrument) + old Step 9 (Observe Revert), the `bkit-debug-observe-instrument` / `bkit-debug-observe-revert` subagents, and the `attempt == 2 → OBSERVE` decision; steps renumber to **10** (1 Start, 2 Worktree, 3 Run Tests, 4 Fetch, 5 Diagnose, 6 Remediate, 7 Soak, 8 Push, 9 Summary, 10 Close). (2) SOAK is entered three ways — invocation start (`DEBUG_ATTEMPT` >= `MAX_DEBUG_ATTEMPT` or `[soak]`), the Step-5 diagnose `Mode: SOAK` signal mid-run, or **NORMAL-loop exhaustion** (all three STANDARD → PIVOT → FINAL strategies fail), a final escalation that previously routed straight to handover. (3) SOAK gets its own counter `SOAK_ATTEMPT`, reset to 0 on **every** SOAK entry and bounded by `MAX_SOAK_ATTEMPT` (= 3) — revising DE-24 refinement (2), where a mid-run fast-track shared the spent inner-loop budget; worst case is now NORMAL (up to 3) + SOAK (up to 3). (4) SOAK prompt hardened: the resolving fix pass MUST strip every `[DEBUG-OBSERVE]` line before `Verdict` = PASS (no-leak). (5) a Close-Workflow **no-leak assertion** fails the run if any added `[DEBUG-OBSERVE]` line survives the debug diff (outside `docs/plans/`), checked via `git diff origin/dev..HEAD` so the bkit-managed prompt/command files that quote the literal marker never false-trip — also closing a pre-existing hole (DE-24's Step-9 marker gate ran only under OBSERVE, never under SOAK). **(2026-06-07 refinement)** the inner-loop counters were renamed to mode-matched pairs for clarity: `TEST_ATTEMPT` → `NORMAL_ATTEMPT` / `MAX_NORMAL_ATTEMPT` (NORMAL loop) and the SOAK bound `MAX_DEBUG_ATTEMPT` → `MAX_SOAK_ATTEMPT`; the invocation pair `DEBUG_ATTEMPT` / `MAX_DEBUG_ATTEMPT` is unchanged. `/bkit-build` and `/bkit-ship` keep `TEST_ATTEMPT` (no NORMAL/SOAK modes there).
- **Why:** "needs added instrumentation to see runtime behaviour" correlates hard with "non-localisable / runtime bug" — exactly SOAK's domain — so a separate, count-triggered, blind-instrumenting, brittle-capture OBSERVE rung carried real cost (mandatory instrument-then-gated-revert on every 2nd debug run, turning easy fixes fragile) without distinct value. #143's own "Concrete suggestion" proposed one soak mode + two gates, never a separate observe mode; OBSERVE (`instrument`/`analyse`) was pre-existing baggage from the old `off|instrument|analyse` enum that #143 built on top of rather than rationalised. Folding it in is net deletion (2 subagents, 2 steps, the OBSERVE attempt trigger) plus one correctness fix (the universal no-leak gate). Fresh SOAK budget on entry is required because the NORMAL-exhaustion → SOAK route would otherwise hand SOAK a spent `NORMAL_ATTEMPT` and starve it immediately.
- **Source:** human
- **Related:** #143, DE-24 (revises), `.bkit/core/workflows/bkit-debug.md` (Steps renumbered 1-10; Step 3 Run-Tests routing incl. NORMAL-exhaustion → SOAK; Step 5 diagnose `Mode: SOAK` budget reset; Step 7 soak `SOAK_ATTEMPT`; Step 10 no-leak assertion), `.bkit/workflows.md` + `.bkit/prompts.md` (catalogs), `.bkit/core/prompts/bkit-debug-failure-soak.md` (no-leak hardening), `.bkit/comparison.md`
rationale: "needs added instrumentation to see runtime behaviour" correlates hard with "non-localisable / runtime bug" — exactly SOAK's domain — so a separate, count-triggered, blind-instrumenting, brittle-capture OBSERVE rung carried real cost (mandatory instrument-then-gated-revert on every 2nd debug run, turning easy fixes fragile) without distinct value. #143's own "Concrete suggestion" proposed one soak mode + two gates, never a separate observe mode; OBSERVE (`instrument`/`analyse`) was pre-existing baggage from the old `off|instrument|analyse` enum that #143 built on top of rather than rationalised. Folding it in is net deletion (2 subagents, 2 steps, the OBSERVE attempt trigger) plus one correctness fix (the universal no-leak gate). Fresh SOAK budget on entry is required because the NORMAL-exhaustion → SOAK route would otherwise hand SOAK a spent `NORMAL_ATTEMPT` and starve it immediately.

summary: #274 — GH Packages auth moves to pnpm user-level config; Vercel `installCommand` shim is not a DE-3/BAR-164 regression
description:
- **Category:** infra
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** The `@cbartens/bkit` registry auth token no longer lives in the committed project `.npmrc` (which now carries ONLY `@cbartens:registry=https://npm.pkg.github.com`). It is written into pnpm's user-level config via `pnpm config set "//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=$BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL"` on every surface that runs `pnpm install`: CI (a step before install), local dev (run once), and Vercel (via a `vercel.json` `installCommand: pnpm config set //npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=$BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL && pnpm install`).
- **Why:** pnpm's auth-handling rework (regression boundary between 10.34.1 and 10.34.3, confirmed live) stopped honouring a project-`.npmrc` `${BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL}` env-substitution at install fetch time — `pnpm install`/`add` 401s (`ERR_PNPM_FETCH_401`) even with the token set (metadata `pnpm view` still resolves, masking it). Config precedence (project `.npmrc` > user config) means a leftover project auth line would also shadow the user-level token, so the token must be _relocated_, not duplicated. `pnpm config set` is version-aware — it writes `~/.npmrc` on pnpm 10.x and `~/.config/pnpm/auth.ini` on pnpm 11.x — so the same command is correct across pnpm majors (preferred over a hand-written `~/.npmrc`). Unblocks #273 (pnpm 10.34.3) and the pnpm-11 migration (#176).
- **Not a regression of DE-3 / DE-11(BAR-164):** DE-3 removed a _git-auth_ installCommand (`git config --global url."…x-access-token…".insteadOf`), obsolete once bkit left git-dep — no git ceremony returns here. DE-11/BAR-164 removed the `setup-auth@v1` _composite action_ (`uses: cbartens/bkit/.github/actions/setup-auth@v1`), which a cross-org private consumer cannot resolve via the runner-scoped `GITHUB_TOKEN` — this is a plain shell command in `vercel.json`, no `uses:` reference, and does not trip the `scanForeignBkitUses` guard. The new Vercel `installCommand` is a minimal registry-auth shim required only because the env-substitution path DE-3 leaned on broke.
- **Discarded:** (1) Keep the project `.npmrc` `_authToken` line as belt-and-suspenders — rejected: it shadows the user-level token and still 401s. (2) Hand-write `~/.npmrc` in CI — rejected: misses pnpm 11's `auth.ini`. (3) Pin Vercel to pnpm <10.34.3 — rejected: fragile (Vercel auto-bumps pnpm).
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** #274, #273, #176, DE-3, DE-11, KN-CORE-7, `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml`, `.bkit/src/bkit-postinstall.ts` (detectNpmrcAuth, detectNpmrcLegacyAuthToken, detectCiYmlMissingTokenEnv)
- **Current (checked 2026-09-23):** Token names carry the `BKIT_` prefix (see `de-35-token-scheme-split-gh-bkit-token-general-write-vs-gh`).
