The Supabase example gates on the docker daemon because `command -v supabase` passes once a provision recipe installs the CLI while the container runtime is absent, and `supabase start || log` would swallow the failure into one stderr line. Reasons moved out of the hook comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Presence check on GH_TOKEN — rejected: misdiagnoses a placeholder token.

summary: Install/upgrade render choices in the install engine: gateway-keyed § Models, no opencode provider default, Codex agents emit no tools/sandbox_mode, self-bump re-execs the new binary, upgrade re-renders output and re-pins, check scopes to installed modules
description: `.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/` and `.bkit/core/engine/render/`: § Models is keyed on gateway; effort ladders on program; an installed `.opencode/` with no recorded provider exits 1; Codex TOML agents carry no `tools:` or `sandbox_mode`; the opencode command anchor carries `$ARGUMENTS`; Cursor commands get the frontmatter description as their first line; `bkit upgrade --to/--latest` installs then re-execs; upgrade re-renders host agents/commands, `.bkit/*.md` docs and package.json gate scripts for installed hosts only and refreshes canonicalHashes + pinnedVersion unconditionally; `bkit check` resolves the opencode provider from the install and scopes drift to sentinel-detected modules; compliance grading resolves parentSha to a hex SHA.
rationale: Gateway keying stops § Models growing as programs x gateways, since a model id belongs to the gateway serving it. Rendering a provider-less opencode install against a substitute would silently rewrite every agent pin to a provider the consumer never chose; calling the resolver speculatively would fail consumers who never installed opencode. Falling back on an unknown effort program would emit a ladder the caller never chose. Codex has no per-agent tool allowlist (openai/codex#6049) and `sandbox_mode` would be `workspace-write` for every write-capable bkit agent, discriminating nothing, so the limitation is documented in providers.md instead of hidden behind a field that only looks restrictive. A stray triple-quote in a prompt would close the TOML value early. Without the `$ARGUMENTS` anchor the opencode command body replaced the user's input and lost the issue ref (#278). Dropping the Cursor description outright let the managed-version marker stand in as the description (#386). Re-exec matters because the running process is the OLD code, and rendering new templates with old logic is a correctness hole; coupling bump and re-render makes it impossible to strand a base branch's mirrors (#256). Without the upgrade re-render a version bump shipped new config but stale prompts/agents/docs; without the unconditional re-pin a clean upgrade left the pin stale and failed the CI drift gate (#129 §3). Without the installed-provider fallback an openrouter/opencode consumer reported false drift on check (#255 #8); without installed-module scoping a single-host repo reported the absent host's files as drift (#252). An unresolved parentSha made every diff-based rule grade an empty diff and pass vacuously, and collapsed compliance history into one identity; the earlier stats.jsonl scan for a workflow-started row could never match, so every row recorded HEAD~1. Upgrade renders opencode.json like install because the json deep-merge otherwise injected raw sentinel keys (#245). Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: `bkit telemetry migrate` maps legacy status/severity/superseded by substring, keys on a truncation-safe slug, keeps friction workflow/step, skips each absent .md pair independently, treats a fresh repo as a clean no-op, and slugs `repo` from the git remote only
description: `.bkit/src/bkit-telemetry-migrate.ts`: legacy Status/superseded spellings map by substring; `partially-resolved` → OPEN; legacy severity `normal` and missing severity → MEDIUM; keys embed the legacy id and append a digest only on truncation; friction rows keep the legacy workflow/step; an absent `.md` skips only its pair; no legacy ledgers and no rows → nothing-to-migrate; issues.jsonl and completed.md count in the already-migrated / legacy-ledger checks; the bootstrap seed runs on every migrate; `repo` comes from the git remote, else `unknown/repo`.
rationale: An exact-equality status check silently defaulted prose like `RESOLVED — closed by …` to OPEN, marking closed work outstanding, and an exact superseded match reported real legacy spellings as ACTIVE; sharing the rule with the friction builder keeps the two from drifting. `normal` is the middle of a three-point scale; missing severity is an explicit unknown->neutral mapping to re-triage on next touch. Embedding the legacy id is safe because migration is a one-shot deterministic read, so two runs cannot race for a number. A 60-char truncated slug is not unique — titles diverging after char 60 collapse to one key and `fold()` keeps only the last, which hits recurrence entries hardest; short titles keep a readable key. Stripping the leading date from a heading would re-key the row so a re-migration mints new entities. Stamping `migrate` as workflow/step would put migrated friction rows on a different axis from live ones and blind the harvest's workflow/step slices. Gating idempotency on jsonl-non-empty aborted the whole run for any consumer missing one legacy pair. Without the fresh-repo check the run fell through to `abort(knowledge.md not found)` and printed `migrate failed` for a documented no-op. Without issues.jsonl in the rows-exist signal a completed.md-only consumer re-ran as nothing-to-migrate, and omitting completed.md from legacy ledgers stranded its rows. The bootstrap seed exists so the roadmap projection has rows for work already in flight on day one, and re-runs so FIDs added after the first migrate get seeded. package.json `name` differs from the slug by one character, and since `repo` is in identity() that forks every entity; a wrong-but-plausible slug forks silently while `unknown/repo` is visible. The one non-throwing JSONL parse primitive bounds the parse-miss class to one place instead of a log-and-continue catch per call site. Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: Ledger schema choices in bkit-telemetry.ts: TRIAGED state, closed deferral reason enum with adjudicator-only `unjustified`, exhaustive deferral writer set, separate `subagent` and `step`, challenge-prompt severity vocabulary, cumulative failure count, `shippedAt`, scrubbed git env, numeric ts coercion
description: `.bkit/core/engine/ledgers/telemetry.ts`: triage ladder OPEN → TRIAGED → CLOSED; `reason` on deferrals is a closed enum (scope-declared / hard-blocked / needs-decision / own-cycle, plus adjudicator-only unjustified that later rows carry verbatim); DEFERRAL writer set excludes the plan executor and gaps-remediator; rows carry both `step` and `subagent`; severity reuses the challenge prompts' four levels; outcome rows carry a cumulative distinct-failure count; feature rows may carry a historic `shippedAt`; repo slug resolution scrubs hook git env vars; `ts` sorting coerces ISO strings; the telemetry summary compares against a rolling median.
rationale: Analysing and fixing are different events, often months apart: without TRIAGED a sweep that works out what an entry is must either lie with CLOSED or discard the analysis with OPEN, and collapsing them loses the interval. Before the reason enum, being declared was the only test for exemption and the agent wanting out of the work wrote its own declaration, so unfinished in-scope work looked identical to genuine out-of-scope work; a closed enum makes the claim testable, and a ledger row being the only place scope was ever declared is the tell. `unjustified` is never rewritten because the discipline rate measures how often an agent deferred work it should have done, not whether someone cleaned up after. The writer set is data because the prose contract alone did not hold: the executor wrote deferral rows despite an explicit NO out-of-scope deferral line, turning blocked in-scope work into something the build loop treats as settled. Conflating `step` and `subagent` costs the harvest a slice dimension and makes which-agent-causes-rework unanswerable. Sharing the challenge prompts' severity lets remediate pass it through without re-deriving. A per-run failure count would mark every run after the first-ever bug as an error run forever. `shippedAt` exists because append-time `ts` makes a backfilled historic ship sort as newest and evict genuinely recent ships. Hook-exported GIT_DIR / GIT_WORK_TREE make `git -C` answer for the hook's repo, so a harvest from a hook would stamp every consumer's rows with bkit's slug. `a.ts - b.ts` on a string ts is NaN, voiding the sort and making fold winners depend on file order. The median is outlier-robust and durations are right-skewed. Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: `bkit:gate:*` names spell their tier chain; only static/unit/format/ship gates are seeded; deeper gates exist only when the consumer declares them; build stops at integration; ci.yml calls tool scripts directly
description: `.bkit/core/engine/install/manifest.ts` BKIT_GATE_SCRIPTS: each gate chains its parent with tier names from the ci.yml job ids; the integration / e2e / live gates are never seeded; `/bkit-build` runs at most `bkit:gate:static-unit-integration`; `/bkit-debug` runs the deepest declared gate; husky templates run the same names; ci.yml does not; `lint:slop` is in no gate; detectGateAdvisories advises a repo that has a deeper tier but no gate for it.
rationale: Name and value describing the same sequence cannot disagree, a caller reads coverage off the name without opening package.json, and `scope` in status.jsonl is self-describing. Husky and agents running the same names means one edit changes both and they cannot drift. ci.yml needs per-step reporting, affected-package conditionals and tiers the local gate excludes, so it calls scripts directly. A seeded `pnpm test:integration` would hard-fail every repo without that tier, and an empty or stub value exits 0 so the workflow records a scope claiming coverage it never ran — the false-green #437 exists to kill; absence is load-bearing, which makes discoverability the problem the advisory solves. Build stops at integration because its diagnose → remediate loop can only repair what its own gate runs: a CI-only tier means build closes green, the PR reds and recovery needs a separate `/bkit-debug`; integration catches contract breaks the unit tier cannot at a cost the loop absorbs, while E2E (a production build plus a browser on every remediation attempt, minutes before CI runs the same on the PR) does not pay for itself. The static gate serves the plan-execute loop and the pre-push revert path, where the tree is knowingly inconsistent and the suite would fail on deletions it cannot fix. The Cursor GateGuard has no failClosed because an advisory hook that fails closed would block the edit it only meant to comment on. The Claude guardrails engine is never wired to a permissionDecision because that would turn an advisory into the blanket prompt the host removed; the Codex wiring text is separate because Cursor's wording names the wrong result and stdout shape and would wire a hook that silently never gates. Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Seed deeper gates as stubs — rejected: false green. Run E2E in the build loop — not adopted: cost per remediation attempt.

summary: Phase-3 detectors: stale-render gates block only on main/dev (or PRs into them), fail safe when the branch is unknown, run after the Phase-2 re-stamp; managed-doc set comes from the package template tree; ci.yml drift is presence-only; @live/@smoke home check runs only where the convention is active
description: `.bkit/core/engine/checks/after/`: detectManagedStale (`managed.ts`, which replaced detectRenderedPromptsStale / detectManagedDocsStale, 802d94f4) is a blocker on main/dev and an advisory elsewhere; an undeterminable branch counts as protected; it runs in Phase 3 so install/upgrade re-stamps first; managed docs are enumerated from `<templates>/docs`; the capstone drift check flags missing known-good fragments only and reads comment-stripped code; the tagged-test home check fires only when some package declares the script; owned-hook-missing fails check; alias collisions are advisory; Vercel installCommand and ci.yml token wiring are checked by raw regex; the BKIT_GH_TOKEN advisory is skipped in CI and without a github MCP server.
rationale: A stale render is almost never created by a feature branch; it is inherited from a dev where the package was bumped without an atomic re-render, so hard-failing every feature push for inherited drift was friction; main/dev stay hard blockers because stale doctrine must never land there, and the PR-into re-assertion keeps the skew from reaching a protected branch silently. An unknown branch must never silently downgrade the gate. Phase-3 placement avoids the chicken-and-egg where the gate would abort the install that fixes it. Globbing the consumer's docs/ would false-positive on every plan, since plans inherit the plan template's bkit:start block. ci.yml is freely edited, so a differs-from-canonical check would be all false positives, while a copy can silently lose a load-bearing invariant and reintroduce a fixed bug (the concurrency-cancel that killed a push-only @live canary); raw-text matching would pass any ci.yml seeded from the commented template. The tag check is convention-gated to stay silent on repos and incidental strings not using it; the capstone `live_ran > 0` assertion is the runtime backstop and this catches it earlier (#483 ghost-green). A deleted owned hook turns its guard off without a word because hook commands skip missing files. Alias collisions are pre-existing ledger data, not an install fault. The Vercel check closes the gap the #274 → 4.1.2 revert papered over (env var checked, installCommand never). A token advisory in CI would be log noise. The stub sentinel needs the full header form so prose back-references cannot fire an undismissable advisory. `bkit-decide` is invisible to the CI-Dispatch Gate, which then reports no-ci on every build and loses its ability to catch an undispatched run. Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Hard-block stale renders on every branch — rejected: inherited drift friction.

summary: The Claude web setup script flips workspace trust and seeds `~/.claude/settings.json` autoMode with `//=`; cloud-bootstrap re-checks trust at the discovered root
description: `.bkit/core/engine/install/cloud-env.ts` renders `@@CLOUD_WORKSPACE_TRUST@@` (merge-write `hasTrustDialogAccepted` for the baked repo path) and `@@CLOUD_USER_SETTINGS@@` (autoMode environment entries led by `$defaults`, seeded with `//=`). The registrable base of a provider baseURL is the naive last two labels. The egress fingerprint hashes derived bases and hosts only.
rationale: Allow rows grant capability, so Claude Code ignores them until trust is accepted, never shows the dialog in `claude -p`/SDK sessions, and announces it only on stderr — config that reads as configured and does nothing. The setup script is the only reliable place: cloud-bootstrap.sh is too late (settings resolve before SessionStart) and an in-session write cannot touch the protected `.claude/` path. The baked clone path is an observation, not a contract; baking plus discovery means a relocated clone costs one degraded session instead of a permanent silent no-op. The classifier deliberately ignores repo-level autoMode so a checked-in repo cannot inject its own allow rules, so bkit cannot ship it in-repo. Unconfigured, every context-fetch host is external, `Host containment` describes an open-internet machine (wrong behind an egress allowlist), and requests for the host's own credentials are blocked. `//=` never stomps a consumer's entries; the trade is that later bkit changes do not reach containers that already have them, the safer direction. Omitting `$defaults` discards every built-in trust slot. Base rewrites for public suffixes would silently widen or narrow a grant, while a registry-gate deny fails loudly. Hosts join the fingerprint because the Cursor paste is hosts-only. `apexBasesOf` stays a named export in install/cloud-env.ts because inlining it into the integration-only install/modules/ would erode the unit coverage floor. Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Write trust from cloud-bootstrap.sh — rejected: too late. Ship autoMode in-repo — impossible: ignored by design.

summary: Each program is pinned to the gateway whose subscription is already paid; no gateway override. Uninstall strips settings arrays element-wise, deletes husks, clears the package.json `bkit` block, and upgrade keeps the drift hash on whole-file skips
description: There is no PROGRAM_GATEWAYS table (removed, 6d1c82d7): claude, cursor and codex each run on their own gateway, and opencode names one with `--opencode=<provider>`. `.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/uninstall.ts` strips array entries element-wise, deletes a markdown file reduced to a lone heading or a residual equal to the stripped template, removes `.codex/agents/bkit-*.toml`, and removes the `bkit` package.json object. `.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/upgrade.ts` resolves write strategy like install, never block-merges byte-equal-text, records a whole-file skip's hash only when disk equals template.
rationale: Pinning is policy, not capability: Cursor and OpenRouter can reach Claude models, but each program uses the subscription already paid for, and when one runs dry the escape is switching program, because the cheap gateway is attached to a different program. Whole-array uninstall equality left the WebFetch-enriched `allow` array behind while stripping `deny`/`ask`, leaving a repo strictly more permissive after uninstall. Lone-heading and template-equal residuals are bkit-authored husks (zero footprint). An extension-only filter would leave every Codex TOML agent behind. Globbing covers new scripts. Clearing the `bkit` object stops an uninstalled repo advertising prior choices. Install and upgrade must never disagree on a file and fight across runs; block-merging a byte-equal-text file would reformat it and churn forever against install. Recording a hash over consumer drift would erase the drift record (#459). Reseeding noise.md instead of moving it would strand every recorded downgrade in warnings.md. `--help` after a verb prints usage because users expect subcommand help. Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Gateway override in Model Overrides — not adopted.

summary: Reasons behind `bkit <noun> <verb>` behaviours: signal-driven evidence clamp with a hard ceiling, roadmap without tracker issues, body-only skip-ci check, runtime probing limits, CI-dispatch lane-namespace match, protect-main binds admins and leaves dev open, exit 126/127 not a test failure, retired-path advisories, context-migrate marker swap and file deletion, alias-collision lint severities
description: `.bkit/core/engine/commands/**` and helpers: `bkit context clamp` keeps signal lines plus head/tail under a 12000-line / 1.5 MB ceiling; `bkit roadmap fold` renders no tracker issues and ranks SHIPPED on shippedAt; the skip-ci body check ignores the subject; `bkit runtime` probes only gh auth and treats `CI=false` as not-CI; the CI-Dispatch probe matches the capstone's lane namespace; `bkit setup protect-main` binds admins and leaves dev unprotected; `bkit tests run` records exit 126/127 as never-ran; `bkit-launch` execs the binary directly; locks refuse a feature split across month buckets; branch rebase union-resolves friction.jsonl.
rationale: Failure signal in local test output is flat or middle-weighted (102 consumer artifacts): head+tail kept as little as 10% of it, signal lines kept 100% while cutting 41–76% of bytes; the ceiling exists because signal immunity alone fails open exactly when things are worst, and over-matching only keeps more lines. A regenerated tracker list can only go stale and a wired tracker already shows the issues; a backfilled row would otherwise evict real recent ships. The defect is a squash body inheriting branch subjects' tokens, while subject `[skip ci]` is a docs-commit convention. gh auth is the flaky probe; `git push --dry-run` never fires a protected branch's hook, so a false true could strand a live session on dev; reading `CI=false` as ambiguous would cost a laptop its worktrees. One lane name breaks on rename and any-check counts Vercel/Renovate as CI. Agents act with the owner's admin token, so an admin exemption makes the agent the bypass; dev operators own that tests ran. Recording a never-ran gate as FAIL sends a debug loop chasing tests that never executed. Nothing else would tell a consumer a retired path call fails. A verbatim config.md move would leave markers nothing parses; matching only `context-fetch:` would strand `debug-fetch:` blocks forever; with no retired-file sweep, a leftover config.md would still read as authoritative. A legacy-seeded ledger pattern-teaches agents to keep minting numbered keys; minted keys only WARN because the one-shot migration legitimately produced them; counting references would invent collisions from cross-links; re-keying unique numbers would churn valid citations. `open -a` routes through launchd, which drops the inherited env (#279/#280). Either month bucket would be a guess. Union can resurrect a drained friction row, but the next harvest re-banks it while a blocking conflict halts the workflow. A slop-scan upgrade that drops a summary field would silently disable the gate; the failure text names the fixes agents reach for first because those make code worse while turning the gate green. Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The Renovate example lists `.bkit/templates/**` and `.agents/skills/**` in `ignorePaths`
description: Workflows copied out of `.bkit/templates/` stay out of `ignorePaths` so their action pins refresh.
rationale: Those trees are bkit-owned and rewritten by bkit; scanning them only produces onboarding noise. A packageRule `enabled: false` does not stop the github-actions manager scanning a file and applying `pinDigests`, so `ignorePaths` is the only way to keep Renovate off it. Reasons moved out of the Renovate example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The Renovate example carries a commented `hostRules` read token for npm.pkg.github.com; Mend uses a repository secret, self-hosted uses the workflow's RENOVATE_HOST_RULES
description: `hostRules` with `token: "{{ secrets.BKIT_GH_TOKEN_INSTALL }}"` is commented out in `.bkit/templates/.github/renovate.json5`.
rationale: Renovate resolves the whole workspace to regenerate the lockfile; without a read token for npm.pkg.github.com the regeneration 401s and CI then fails `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. The block stays commented so the self-hosted workflow's env auth is not doubled. Reasons moved out of the Renovate example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The Renovate example puts every auto-mergeable non-major npm bump in one PR and gives each multi-package ecosystem one lockstep PR for majors only
description: Dev minor/patch, prod patch, `@types/**` and the eslint family share `groupName: "non-major dependencies"`; `@types/**` and eslint rules are scoped to minor/patch; `@tanstack/**`, `vitest*`/`@vitest/**` and `@playwright/**` have major-only groups.
rationale: Every Renovate PR rewrites pnpm-lock.yaml, so several PRs firing in the same window force serial rebases and stall `platformAutomerge`; one shared group means one weekly lockfile change, one merge, no rebase cascade. The `@types` and eslint pattern rules carry no update-type filter otherwise, so without the minor/patch scope a major bump would join the auto-merge group instead of falling to the majors rule. A coordinated breaking bump (e.g. `@tanstack/react-query` + `@tanstack/query-core`) must land together; without the major-scoped group each package would get its own PR and the halves would fail CI against each other. Reasons moved out of the Renovate example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's own CI honours `[skip ci]` / `[skip actions]` only from a push commit message, never from a PR title
description: `Read Markers` in `.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` (bkit repo only) feeds `SKIP_MSG` only when `EVENT_NAME` is `push`; a pull_request title is read for force markers but never for skip markers.
rationale: A PR-title skip would turn off `bkit-tests-check`, bkit's sole required branch-protection check, so a PR could reach a merge with no suite run. Reasons moved out of `.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's own CI recognises `[force full]` and maps it to run_level=full, the same as `[force build]`
description: `Read Markers` and `Decide Run Level` in `.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` (bkit repo only) accept `[force full]`; it yields `run_level=full` with `source=marker:force-full`. In the consumer scaffold it additionally bypasses `web_affected` (integration + e2e + @live).
rationale: bkit is one package with no deploy and no affected-graph, so `[force full]` has nothing extra to bypass here; it is recognised only so the consumer-scaffold marker is exercised in bkit's own CI. Reasons moved out of `.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's CI static lane and the cloud claude job install a pinned, checksum-verified vale tarball
description: `Install Vale` in `.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` (vale 3.9.1, sha256-checked, then `vale sync` with three attempts) and `Install vale` in the claude job of `.github/workflows/bkit-cloud.yml` / `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-cloud.yml` (same version and checksum).
rationale: vale is not on GitHub's runner image and `.vale/styles/` is gitignored, so without an explicit install `lint:prose` soft-skips (see `f9-lint-prose-restores-vale-styles-soft-skips-only-missing-binary`) and the prose gate is silently off in CI; in the cloud job, cloud-bootstrap.sh's `vale sync` and the dispatched phase's lint:prose would also no-op, unlike the cloud.md web env whose setup script installs vale. Reasons moved out of `ci.yml` and `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's own CI runs the Tier-3 status-hole detector on every static lane, fail-open
description: `Check Status Holes` in `bkit-tests-static` (`.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml`, bkit repo only) runs `pnpm bkit:audit:status || true`; the CLI exits 0 even when it finds holes.
rationale: `384-tier3-promotion` promotes the detector to a blocking gate only after one release of fail-open signal without muting, and that signal accrues only if something runs it. `|| true` is a second guard; the CLI's own contract is exit 0 always. Reasons moved out of `.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's unit coverage is scoped by an explicit `--coverage.include` list passed on the CLI; the bkit-modules data registry is outside it
description: `--coverage.include` in the `test:coverage:unit` script (`package.json`) lists named logic files under `.bkit/core/engine/` (`{cli,commands/analysis,install/cloud-env,...}`); the integration-only `install/modules/*` are not listed. The branch floor `--coverage.thresholds.branches` sits just below current and is ratcheted up.
rationale: The bkit-modules data registry is exercised end-to-end by integration tests, not unit-tested. vitest coverage is per run, not per project, so the scope has to be a CLI flag on the run. No reason is recorded for leaving out the other four files. Reasons moved out of `.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's own CI runs unit and integration tests as separate parallel jobs, each with its own coverage number and executed-count
description: `bkit-tests-unit` and `bkit-tests-integration` in `.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` (bkit repo only) are parallel siblings of `bkit-tests-static`; each emits `tests_ran`, and `bkit-tests-check` asserts each lane executed >0 tests. e2e / migrate / live lanes exist only in the consumer template.
rationale: Separate lanes give each tier its own honest coverage number and executed-count, mirror how consumers (consumer-a, consumer-b) run their tiers, and exercise the per-tier `bkit-stub:coverage` scaffold shipped to consumers. Reasons moved out of `.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit's integration coverage is report-only and scoped to the engine surface; the lane is gated on execution, not a percentage
description: `Run Integration Tests` in `.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` (bkit repo only) passes `--coverage.include='.bkit/core/engine/{install/modules/*,commands/install/install,commands/install/upgrade,commands/install/uninstall}.ts'` and no `--coverage.thresholds`; `bkit-tests-check` requires `integration_ran > 0`.
rationale: A hard integration percentage punishes the correct test-pyramid shape (testing.md § Coverage on PRs). Scoping to the engine surface makes the number reflect the flows integration tests are meant to drive, not a whole-repo denominator. Reasons moved out of `.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: `bkit_dev_dispatch_guard` picks the FID's status directory with a sorted `find`
description: `status_dir=$(find docs/plans ... -path "docs/plans/*/logs/$guard_fid" | sort | head -1)` in the `context` job of `bkit-cloud.yml`.
rationale: An unsorted `find` takes readdir order, so a FID whose logs span two YYYYMM buckets could read the cap counter from one file and write it to another across cycles, silently unbounding the cap. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: `bkit_dev_dispatch_guard` refuses to dispatch when the FID's status.jsonl cannot be parsed; only an absent file counts as zero
description: In the `context` job of `bkit-cloud.yml`, a failing `jq -s` over the status file returns 1 with `::notice::... is unparseable — refusing to dispatch ... uncounted (fail-closed)`.
rationale: A truncated line, stray non-JSON row or merge=union conflict artefact must not degrade to `dev_count=0`, which would defeat the cap entirely. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The dev-dispatch landing check wraps `git show` in its own `|| true` before piping to jq
description: `landed=$( (git -C "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE" show "origin/dev:${status_file}" 2>/dev/null || true) | jq -s ... || echo 0)` in the `context` job of `bkit-cloud.yml`.
rationale: Under pipefail, a failing `git show` (row never landed) plus a succeeding jq that prints `0` makes the pipeline fail, firing `|| echo 0` a second time; `$landed` becomes a two-line value that breaks the `-lt` comparison and bypasses the fail-closed check. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The dev arm's commit-scope FID regex accepts both GitHub (`363-slug`) and Linear (`bar-123-slug`) shapes
description: `grep -oE '^\w+\((([0-9]+|[a-z]+-[0-9]+)-[a-z0-9-]+)\):'` in the `context` job of `bkit-cloud.yml`, the same alternation as the feat/** fallback. The kill switch (`gh issue view`) is GitHub-Issues-only, so a Linear FID no-ops there.
rationale: Kept for forward-compatibility with a future MCP-based kill switch, not as a present end-to-end guarantee: the workflow's kill switch and permissions are GitHub-Issues-only, so the dev trigger does not work for Linear-tracker consumers today. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The dev arm's linked-PR FID fallback reads only same-repo MERGED PRs, matching the repo via `env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY` inside `--jq`
description: `gh api repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/commits/${HEAD_SHA}/pulls --jq '[.[] | select(.head.repo.full_name == env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY and .merged_at != null)] | .[0].body // empty'` in the `context` job of `bkit-cloud.yml`.
rationale: The endpoint returns PRs associated with the commit, which for a dev commit includes OPEN fork PRs branched at that SHA; the job-level `head_repository` guard gates the trigger, not this lookup, so an unfiltered `.[0]` would let an outsider's PR body choose the FID this trusted job dispatches against. The legitimate feature PR is merged and same-repo by construction. The repo name is read through `env.` because `gh api` has no `--arg`, and splicing it into the filter text would be injectable. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit-cloud.yml's kill switch matches the `bkit:auto` label exactly (`grep -qxF`), never as a substring
description: Every `gh issue view "$ISSUE" --json labels --jq '.labels[].name' | grep -qxF 'bkit:auto'` check in the `context` job of `bkit-cloud.yml`.
rationale: A substring `grep -q 'bkit:auto'` over the label list also matches `bkit:auto-disabled`, `bkit:auto-paused` or `no-bkit:auto`, defeating the kill switch for an operator who believes such a label revokes automation. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: On the dev arm, the bkit:auto kill switch runs before the stale-run guard and the dispatch-cap guard
description: In the `context` job of `bkit-cloud.yml`, the `gh issue view ... grep -qxF 'bkit:auto'` check precedes `LATEST_CI_SHA` / the stale-run guard and `bkit_dev_dispatch_guard`; it needs nothing they set.
rationale: `bkit_dev_dispatch_guard` mkdir -p's, commits and pushes a telemetry row to dev; in the reverse order, an operator who removed bkit:auto to halt a misbehaving loop would still get bkit-auto[bot] commits pushed to dev on every later red dev CI. The removed comment named the stale-run guard as the writer; that guard now writes only to the run summary. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The dev stale-run guard selects the CI workflow by filename (`--workflow bkit-ci.yml`), not by its display name
description: `gh run list --branch dev --workflow bkit-ci.yml --status completed` in the `context` job of `bkit-cloud.yml`.
rationale: The display name (`CI`) is consumer-editable free text; the filename is fixed. The removed comment said `bkit install` fixes the filename; install no longer writes ci.yml, and the fixed name is now the copy target in `.bkit/templates.md` § Contract. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: When the dev stale-run guard finds no completed CI run, it proceeds and emits a `::warning::` naming the bkit-ci.yml filename requirement
description: `if [ -z "$LATEST_CI_SHA" ]` in the `context` job of `bkit-cloud.yml` writes `::warning::gh run list --branch dev --workflow bkit-ci.yml returned no completed runs — stale-run guard disabled ...`.
rationale: Fail-open is recorded in `363-dev-stale-run-guard-by-ci-recency`; a PERMANENT misconfiguration (the consumer's CI workflow file is not literally ci.yml) looks the same as a transient API failure unless flagged, so the warning stops the guard running disabled for months unnoticed. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The feat/** branch-name fallback keeps the FULL FID slug; ISSUE is derived from it
description: `FID=$(echo "$BRANCH" | sed -E 's#^feat/##')` in the `context` job of `bkit-cloud.yml`; ISSUE (short numeric/alpha prefix, used only for `gh issue view`) is derived from the full FID.
rationale: A truncated FID (e.g. `363` instead of `363-widen-bkit-cloud-trigger`) would count against a different status.jsonl / status_dir key than the dev-path FID, breaking the one-shared-budget-per-FID invariant and orphaning a `docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{truncated}/` directory. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The feat/** arm no-ops while a build is still running on the branch
description: In the `context` job of `bkit-cloud.yml`, if the branch's status.jsonl shows a build `workflow-started` with no later `workflow-done` / `workflow-failed` and its newest build row is under 1800 s old, the `context` job exits with `skip=true`; unreadable status fails open.
rationale: Dispatching debug or ship then would put a second agent on the same branch mid-run. Build pushes before opening its PR, so this fires only when a PR from an earlier attempt is still open. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The opencode job installs opencode at a pinned version
description: `npm install -g @opencode/cli@2.0.26` in `Install opencode` of `bkit-cloud.yml`: 2.0.x ships only on npm, so the `https://opencode.ai/install` curl installer (GitHub release binaries) cannot fetch it. No updater bumps the pin.
rationale: A bare `| bash` installs whatever opencode.ai/install resolves as latest at run time: unpinned remote code executing with the runner token. Reasons moved out of `bkit-cloud.yml` comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The self-hosted Renovate example serialises runs and queues rather than cancels
description: `concurrency: { group: renovate, cancel-in-progress: false }` in `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-renovate.yml` and `.github/workflows/bkit-renovate.yml`.
rationale: Two overlapping Renovate processes race on the same renovate/* branches and the Dependency Dashboard issue. Cancelling mid-push can leave a half-written branch or PR, and Renovate is idempotent, so a queued run that supersedes an identical pending one is harmless. Reasons moved out of the renovate.yml example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The self-hosted Renovate example wakes daily at an off-hour minute, never Monday-only
description: `cron: "17 6 * * *"` in `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-renovate.yml` and `.github/workflows/bkit-renovate.yml`; Renovate's own `schedule` in renovate.json5 gates normal update PRs.
rationale: osvVulnerabilityAlerts CVE PRs bypass Renovate's internal schedule and must be able to open on the next daily wake, not once a week. The off-hour minute avoids top-of-hour congestion, and each wake is a fast no-op when nothing is due (Renovate exits in seconds outside its window). Reasons moved out of the renovate.yml example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The self-hosted Renovate example allow-lists `PNPM_*` so the shared renovate.json5 `env:` block is accepted
description: `RENOVATE_ALLOWED_ENV: "PNPM_*"` in `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-renovate.yml` and `.github/workflows/bkit-renovate.yml`; renovate.json5 ships `env: { PNPM_WORKERS, PNPM_MAX_WORKERS }` for both runners.
rationale: renovate.json5 is one config shared by Mend and the self-hosted runner, so the worker-cap env stays in it even though the OOM it mitigates cannot happen on a 16 GB runner; without the allow-list the self-hosted bot rejects the whole config. Reasons moved out of the renovate.yml example's comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: bkit owns only what a workflow step runs or parses; every shipped file is an owned file, an owned part of a shared file, or a template
description: **Owned file** — install and upgrade overwrite it; uninstall removes it while it still matches its `.bkit/version` hash: workflow, prompt, agent and command copies, `docs/templates/bkit-plan.md` and `docs/templates/bkit-audit-*.md`, `.bkit/.env.example`, and the hook scripts (`.claude/hooks/bkit-*`, `.codex/hooks/bkit-*`, `.cursor/hooks/bkit-*`, `.opencode/plugin/bkit-*.js`). **Owned part of a shared file** — bkit rewrites and removes only its part: markdown between `bkit:start` and `bkit:end` (`AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.agents/rules.md`, `.agents/docs.md`, `.agents/context.md`, `.agents/skills.md`, `.bkit/prompts.md`, `docs/*.md`, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`); hook entries and permissions in `.claude/settings.json`; Cursor and Codex `hooks.json`; `permission`, `plugin`, `mcp` and `provider` in `.opencode/opencode.json`; the tracker entry under `mcpServers` in `.mcp.json` and `.cursor/mcp.json`. The `bkit:gate:*` / `bkit:deps:*` names in `package.json` are added when missing and never rewritten. **Template** — never applied to the repo; raw copies refresh in the consumer's `.bkit/templates/` (the whole `.bkit/templates/` folder, `syncTemplateCopies`, `.bkit/core/engine/install/template-copies.ts`; the slop plugin is one of them), including one context-fetch file per provider under `.bkit/templates/context/`. No file is written once and then hash-tracked: bkit either keeps a file current or leaves it to the consumer. Every owned file and owned block that is not JSON carries the managed-version marker (`489-managed-version-marker-on-every-written-file`).
rationale: A file a workflow step runs or parses has to match the workflows, so bkit keeps it current; a file a person or another tool runs belongs to the consumer's stack, so it ships as a template (issue body). The managed block of `.agents/context.md` holds the marker formats, self-skip contract and `allowed-domains` / `mcp-servers` rules that `/bkit-debug` and install parse, so bkit keeps it current; the ready-made fetch blocks are templates (`489-context-fetch-blocks-are-per-provider-templates`). The write-once, hash, upgrade-conflict and uninstall-reclaim machinery existed only so bkit could claim a consumer's file still matched the installed version; once the consumer decides whether to adopt, that claim is gone (issue body). Hooks stay owned because they enforce what workflows and prompts forbid (force push, `--no-verify`, `git reset --hard`) and change in step with them, so a stale copy runs workflows under old guards with no signal. The JSON keys stay owned because install fills them from install choices (`@@OPENCODE_TRACKER_MCP@@`, `@@OPENCODE_PROVIDER_KEY@@`), the tracker MCP entry is what tracker steps write through, and these files change often (settled plan 2026-10-07 §1). Accepted cost: bkit no longer promises that a consumer's CI, hooks and prose-lint config match the installed version, so workflows must not call those files (`467-workflows-reach-templates-only-via-commands-and-package-json-settings`).
alternatives: The issue body's boundary table, with MCP config and the gate scripts on the template side — rejected in the 2026-10-07 settled plan as too coarse: tracker steps need the tracker MCP entry, workflows run the gate scripts, and the table missed that workflows still called some template files (those calls were removed first, in #467). `.agents/context.md` as create-if-missing (Wave 2a, ef1f09a7) — reversed 2026-10-10 (owner, #489 "Decided (2026-10-10)"): its managed rules would freeze at the version first installed while the code that reads the blocks keeps changing.

summary: Ready-made context-fetch blocks ship as one template per provider in `.bkit/templates/context/`; the managed block of `.agents/context.md` holds only the rules
description: `.bkit/templates/context/` holds one file per provider: `github` (`context=ci` and `context=diff`), `expo` (`context=runtime` and `context=e2e`), `maestro` (`context=e2e`, every failed job matching `MAESTRO_JOB_RE`, iOS and Android lanes), `playwright`, `tavily`, `sentry`, `vercel`, `supabase`, `stripe`, `resend`, `inngest`, `cloudrun`, `serena`. Each file holds that provider's fetch blocks, its `context-fetch:provision` block where a stack CLI is needed, its env vars, the `allowed-domains` lines bkit's egress registry does not already derive, and its `mcp-servers` names. Project names, slugs and ids are placeholders (`your-team-slug`, `your-project-ref`, …) on a commented assignment line or env default, never a consumer's names (`.bkit/templates.md:76-92`, `.bkit/core/engine/audits/templates/context-templates.test.ts`). `syncTemplateCopies` copies them raw, with the rest of `.bkit/templates/`, into the consumer's `.bkit/templates/context/` (`.bkit/core/engine/install/template-copies.ts:49`). The managed block of `.agents/context.md` keeps only the rules — marker formats, contexts, self-skip contract, output bounds, provisioning, `allowed-domains` and `mcp-servers` — and bkit keeps it current. A consumer copies a provider's blocks below `<!-- bkit:end -->` and adds its domains and MCP names to their lists (`.bkit/templates.md:52-102`). The `context-fetch-source-not-enabled` advisory reads block names from these templates and names the file to copy (`shippedContextFetchTemplates`, `.bkit/core/engine/checks/before/context-fetch.ts:221`).
rationale: The managed half of `.agents/context.md` is the rules `/bkit-debug` and install parse; freezing it at first install leaves agents acting on stale rules while the code that reads the blocks moves on, so it stays bkit-owned and current. Examples are not rules, so they are templates the consumer adopts and owns. One file per provider, never one per block or per platform (owner 2026-10-10), because the domains and MCP server names a block needs belong with that block. Folder `.bkit/templates/context/` is the owner's choice over the proposed `context-fetch/` (#489 "Decided (2026-10-10)"). Placeholders keep any one consumer's names out of shipped files (#489 proposal 2026-10-10).
alternatives: (1) `.agents/context.md` create-if-missing, examples kept inside its managed block (Wave 2a, ef1f09a7) — rejected: the rules freeze at the version first installed. (2) Separate allowed-domains and MCP-server templates — rejected: the hosts and servers a block needs belong with that block. (3) Folder `.bkit/templates/context-fetch/` — not adopted (owner, 2026-10-10); no reason recorded.

summary: Every file and block bkit writes or refreshes carries the managed-version marker, except JSON
description: One marker text (`bkit:managed vX.Y.Z — <licence notice> — do not edit; run `bkit upgrade` to refresh`, licence per `507-polyform-notice-travels-with-written-files`) in the file's comment syntax: `<!-- … -->` in markdown, `# <!-- … -->` in shell, `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`, `.env.example` and codex TOML agents, `// …` in JS hooks and `.mjs` scripts. In a markered file it is the first line inside the bkit block; in a whole file it sits below the first heading or frontmatter, or on line 2. Sources carry `{{BKIT_MANAGED_MARKER}}`; the comment prefix in front of the token picks the form (`applyTokens`, `.bkit/core/engine/install/placeholders.ts:103`; `managedVersionMarker`, `readManagedVersion`, `.bkit/core/engine/install/version-file.ts:266-277`). Rendered prompts, agents, commands and skills are stamped at render. JSON files where bkit owns keys carry none. `detectManagedStale` (`bkit-managed-stale`, `.bkit/core/engine/checks/after/managed.ts:132`) checks every stamped file: blocker on main/dev, advisory on feature branches.
rationale: A consumer who bumps the bkit package without re-rendering leaves agents reading stale rules and hooks; the marker lets `bkit check` catch that on every file bkit writes, not only docs and prompts. JSON has no comment syntax. Accepted cost: every release changes every managed file in the consumer's diff.

summary: bkit's own `.bkit/core/.bkit/*.md` doc sources carry the literal `{{BKIT_MANAGED_MARKER}}` line; the installed `.bkit/*.md` copies carry the stamped marker
description: The package doc sources live in `.bkit/core/.bkit/` (`cloud`, `comparison`, `install`, `jsonl`, `prompts`, `providers`, `README`, `templates`, `trackers`, `workflows`) and hold the token, never a version. Install renders them into `.bkit/*.md` with the version marker (`runBkitDocs`, `.bkit/core/engine/install/modules/core.ts:250`), in this repo as in a consumer's.
rationale: A version stamped into a package source would be rewritten on every release and shipped as a hardcoded value.

summary: `.agents/skills.md` is a managed block like `.agents/context.md`; the create-if-missing group is deleted
description: Install and upgrade refresh the block between `<!-- bkit:start -->` and `<!-- bkit:end -->`; content below `bkit:end` (`Project Skills`) is the consumer's; uninstall strips only the block; `bkit check` flags a stale block. `CREATE_IF_MISSING_PATHS` and `writeIfAbsent` are deleted. `bkit skills prune` reads the whole file.
rationale: Owner 2026-10-10: the universal skills table stays current. Accepted cost: a consumer who edited inside the block loses those edits on the first upgrade, and one who removed the markers gets a fresh block appended.

summary: In the template ci.yml, `[force build]` and `[force cache]` make a lane run even when the same commit already passed
description: The `Check SHA Cache` step in `.bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml` skips a lane when the commit passed CI in the last 7 days, unless the commit message or PR title carries `[force build]` or `[force cache]`.
rationale: Without it a re-push of an already-green commit skipped every lane and `[force cache]` did nothing; bkit's own CI already behaved this way.

summary: The `guardrails.cjs` hooks' empty catches are their fail-open contract
rationale: The empty catches implement the hook's fail-open contract: an internal error yields no decision. No further reason is written down. Reason moved out of the slop-scan config comment (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: `bkit telemetry validate` and `normalise` are removed; `telemetry summary` stays
rationale: Both served the retired DE-N/KN-N key numbering. Run against consumer-a, validate reported issue-number prefixes in key names (KN-1210, KN-1219) as collisions.

summary: The version downgrade and stale-pin detectors read `pinnedVersion` from `.bkit/version`
rationale: They read the file as plain text, so they never fired on the JSON format every install writes.

summary: The `.npmrc` `_authToken` advisory (`npmrc-authtoken-line`) stays
rationale: Current hazard, not something an older bkit wrote: GitHub's docs tell people to write that line, and it causes 401s on pnpm >=10.34.3.

summary: One context list and one start-line parser serve the advisories and the `bkit context` runner
rationale: Two copies had drifted. The runner follows the advisories' stricter reading: a malformed start line opens no block.

summary: The template path-reference test takes its names from the files under `.bkit/templates/`; `isTemplate` is gone
rationale: A hand-written list missed seven templates. `bkit-design-review-1` reading `docs/capabilities.md` "when present" is an allowed optional read, held as one narrow allowance.

summary: Uninstall deletes the owned `docs/templates/bkit-*.md` files and strips bkit's blocks from `docs/*.md`
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Decision row 489-own-only-what-a-workflow-runs-four-file-groups wins over the code, which left `docs/` untouched.

summary: `bkit check` warns when a `bkit:gate:*` script is empty or a no-op (`true`, `:`, `exit 0`, `echo …`)
rationale: Owner decision 2026-10-10 on the #467/#489 review. Such a gate checks nothing, and only the gates audit caught it. Warn-only, so a deliberate stub does not block a push.

summary: Workflows write `status.jsonl` and `.bkit/issues.jsonl` rows only through `bkit` commands; no workflow block appends with `>>`
description: Row writers: `workflow-started` / `workflow-failed` / `workflow-done` plus close telemetry → `bkit workflows start|fail|close`; `step-done` → `bkit steps done` (captures `parentSha`, writes the row, then commits, in that order); `workflow-meta` → `bkit status meta` (`--debug-mode` / `--push-mode` / `--debug-attempt` / `--plan-source` / `--soak-entry` / `--opened-pr`); `runtime-resolved` → `bkit runtime row`; `transport-fallback` / `close-transport` → `bkit prs transport-row`; any other typed audit row the fold does not model (ship's gate refusals, CI probes, timeouts, merge CI) → `bkit status row --type=`, which refuses a folded type; `kind:"feature"` rows → `bkit roadmap feature` (appends, re-renders `docs/roadmap.md`, fail-open). Reads go through `bkit status route` and `bkit counters derive|rows|run`; no counter is derived by raw jq over `status.jsonl`. `bkit workflows close` runs in the worktree before the squash in both close modes, so its rows ride the branch. Gates: `ship-invariants.test.ts` (no `>>` onto `status.jsonl` or `.bkit/issues.jsonl` in any phase workflow) and `counter-prose-audit.test.ts` (no raw-jq counter).
rationale: A raw `>>` bypasses the row shape and the fail-open contract the commands own (`ship-invariants.test.ts`). `bkit steps gate` checks the row `steps done` wrote, so a step no longer types its own row and then ticks a box saying it did; `steps done` orders parentSha capture, row and commit because the fold's de-dup key needs `parentSha` to advance per attempt (`.bkit/core/engine/commands/workflow/steps.ts` header). Close rows written in the worktree before the squash ride the branch (045e990f).
alternatives: No rejected alternative is recorded in the #467 commits, `.bkit/workflows.md` or `docs/architecture.md`.

summary: No workflow, prompt or `.bkit/wording.md` names an installed template path; mechanics come from `bkit` commands and settings from `package.json` `bkit`
description: `.bkit/core/engine/audits/templates/template-path-refs.test.ts` fails when a line in `.bkit/core/workflows/*.md`, `.bkit/core/prompts/*.md` or `.bkit/wording.md` names a template path: each `.github/workflows/` template file name, `.husky/`, `.vale`, `.lintstagedrc.json`, `slop-scan.config.json`, `.envrc`, and each `scripts/<tool>/` template folder. The workflow and script names are read from `.bkit/templates/`, so a new template is covered without editing the test. Settings a command needs come from `package.json` `bkit` through one reader, `.bkit/core/engine/shared/settings.ts`: `ciWorkflow` (default `bkit-ci.yml`), `capstoneJob` (default `bkit-tests-check`), `worktree.copy` (default `.env`, `.env.local`), `worktree.install` (default true), `issueTracker`, `githubProject`, `shipGateRequiredLanes` (default empty). No command hard-codes a CI workflow, check name or app folder.
rationale: Templates are the consumer's once installed: they rename, delete or rewrite them (a CI workflow, a hook, a lint config, a helper script), and a workflow step that reads or runs one by path breaks the day the consumer does (`.bkit/core/engine/audits/templates/template-path-refs.test.ts` header). One settings reader gives one set of defaults (`.bkit/core/engine/shared/settings.ts` header).
alternatives: A hand-maintained forbidden-path list in the test — not used: names derive from the templates folder so a new template is covered without editing the test (test header). No other alternative is recorded.

summary: bkit distribution via the public npm registry
rationale: GitHub Packages needs a read token even for a public package, so every remote build surface carried install auth for a devDependency no build imports (#408).
description: `@cbartens/bkit` publishes to the public npm registry (`package.json` `publishConfig`: `registry` `https://registry.npmjs.org/`, `access` `public`). Installs need no token, no `@cbartens:registry` `.npmrc` mapping and no GitHub Packages auth on any surface (local, CI, Vercel, cloud, Renovate). `.github/workflows/release.yml` publishes from CI through npm OIDC trusted publishing (`id-token: write`, `npm publish --provenance`), with no long-lived token. GitHub Packages is no longer updated.

summary: BAR-141 — Structured PreflightFinding replaces printSink
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** Replace `ModuleContext.printSink: string[]` with `ModuleContext.advisories: PreflightFinding[]` (shape: `{id, severity, detect, action}`). Install restructured into three phases: Phase 1 preflight (read-only, blockers short-circuit before any writes), Phase 2 dispatch (unchanged), Phase 3 post-install re-detection (token surfaces, ci.yml, vale sync). Findings deduplicated by `id` — Phase 3 wins on conflict.
- **Why:** `printSink: string[]` was unparseable by downstream tooling, emitted advisory strings during module execution (before post-install state was accurate), and had no structured `id` for deduplication. Structured shape enables: (1) stable `id` registry for downstream automation; (2) blocker short-circuit before any writes; (3) accurate post-install re-detection; (4) unified banner formatter reusable by BAR-139 (`bkit uninstall`).
- **Discarded:** (1) Keep `printSink` + add parallel `findings: PreflightFinding[]` — two sinks → drift risk; downstream tooling has to merge two shapes. (2) `--strict` flag promoting advisories to blockers — out of scope; consumer can use `bkit check` (exit-1-on-drift). (3) Auto-apply advisory fixes — violates consumer-value-wins principle.
- **Source:** phase
- **Related:** BAR-141, `docs/plans/202605/bar-141-preflight-checklist-plan.md`, `.bkit/core/engine/checks/before/index.ts`, `.bkit/core/engine/checks/after/index.ts`, `.bkit/core/engine/commands/install/install.ts`, `.bkit/core/engine/install/modules/`, `.bkit/core/engine/install/write.ts`, DE-3, KN-4
rationale: `printSink: string[]` was unparseable by downstream tooling, emitted advisory strings during module execution (before post-install state was accurate), and had no structured `id` for deduplication. Structured shape enables: (1) stable `id` registry for downstream automation; (2) blocker short-circuit before any writes; (3) accurate post-install re-detection; (4) unified banner formatter reusable by BAR-139 (`bkit uninstall`).

summary: #341 C1/C2 posture landed as specified: actions MCP toolset enabled (C1), gh-hardening prefers sanctioned GH_TOKEN with a loud dual-lane preflight and no second token (C2); which concrete MCP server mode 3 loads (proxy-brokered built-in vs .mcp.json's github server) remains a named residual, deferred to the live WS-16 mode-3 run per design-addendum-spikes.md.
rationale: Spike C (closed) verified the §6c gh->MCP tool names (actions_list/actions_get/get_job_logs/download_workflow_run_artifact) exist on github/github-mcp-server once the `actions` toolset is enabled -- Sub-Plan 1/T4 added it to .mcp.json's X-MCP-Toolsets, closing OQ1's 'no MCP artifact-download tool' gap. Spike C also confirmed the credential-coupling risk (.mcp.json and cloud-bootstrap.sh both read BKIT_GH_TOKEN -- if mode 3 withholds it, gh AND the MCP fallback die together): Sub-Plan 1/T5 hardened cloud-bootstrap.sh to prefer the sanctioned GH_TOKEN env var over --with-token and added a loud gh auth status preflight (never silent), with NO second explicit MCP token introduced (a token-withholding sandbox withholds any second secret too). The decision to prefer the platform's proxy-brokered built-in GitHub MCP in mode 3 (full decoupling from BKIT_GH_TOKEN) over .mcp.json's own github server is confirmed only by a real mode-3 session -- named as a residual (not silently assumed) and owned by T16's Manual Verification Step 2, deferred to a live claude.ai session per the design's own honest limit (D3).
description:
- **Category:** cloud / MCP / auth
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** C1 (enable `actions` MCP toolset) and C2 (decouple fallback auth via sanctioned GH_TOKEN + loud dual-lane preflight, no second token) both landed exactly as design-addendum-spikes.md specified. The one open half of C2 -- which concrete MCP server mode 3 resolves to, and whether it is credential-decoupled from BKIT_GH_TOKEN in practice -- is a residual live-mode-3 observation, not a static-verifiable claim; it is explicitly named (never silently assumed closed) and owned by Sub-Plan 6/T16's live run.
- **Why:** see rationale.
- **Source:** agent (#341 build, Sub-Plan 6/T16 documentation closeout)
- **Related:** #341, design-addendum-spikes.md Decisions C1/C2, spike-findings.md Findings C1/C2, 341-oqa-shape-a-transport-d5a-pr-close-confirmed
alternatives: gh-only CI fallback (no actions toolset) -- REJECTED, leaves the mode-3 CI gate unrecoverable when gh breaks with the token present. A second explicit MCP token -- REJECTED, a token-withholding sandbox withholds any second secret too; adds management surface for no gain.

summary: derive each egress base as the last two labels of the host and gate it with two denylists; no public-suffix-list dependency, no vendored suffix table, and a per-row declaration required only where the gate rejects the default
description: Egress bases are proposed by collapsing a registry entry baseURL host to its last two labels, then judged by a test-only gate: label-boundary suffix match, at least 2 labels, not in MULTI_LABEL_SUFFIXES (co.uk, com.au, ...), not in MULTI_TENANT_APEXES (amazonaws.com, googleapis.com, workers.dev, vercel.app, pages.dev, run.app, ...). A row overrides bases, or declares an empty bases with a recorded reason, only when the gate rejects the derived default. Both denylists live as data in the branch-free leaf .bkit/core/engine/shared/egress.ts; the gate runs in the bkit repo only and never in a consumer install.
rationale: A public suffix list solves the case that barely occurs in AI-provider hosts (example.co.uk) and does NOT solve the case that actually widens egress. Verbatim example, recorded here so it is not rediscovered: bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com collapses to *.amazonaws.com, which is every S3 bucket on the internet, and us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com collapses to *.googleapis.com, which is Drive, Gmail, GCS and IAM to an agent that may hold an ambient cloud token. PSL is the wrong tool for that risk and adds a snapshot dataset needing Renovate bumps. A vendored subset is the same trade minus the bump automation and embeds an unrecorded ICANN-vs-private-section policy. Pure declaration on every entry taxes each provider addition with an answer the machine already knows (all four current derived entries pass the default unchanged); pure derivation has no trip-wire and fails silently in the widening direction. The safety lives in the gate, not in the declaration, so requiring declaration only on gate rejection buys the same guarantee at zero routine cost. The gate is deliberately a DENY, so an unknown platform apex passes; a soft warning on .dev/.app/.run TLDs makes that residual visible without failing the build on a legitimate vendor.
alternatives: psl or tldts as a runtime dependency (rejected: wrong risk, snapshot dataset, bump burden); a hand-copied ICANN subset (rejected: same trade without bump automation, plus an unrecorded section policy); silently narrowing to the raw host on a denylist hit (rejected: a rewriter ships a surprise to every consumer and is invisible in review, whereas a gate fails loud at authoring time); no check at all (rejected: the groq-inherits-nvidia.com copy-paste class and the multi-tenant-apex over-grant class both ship silently)

summary: derive the shipped egress set from every entry of every shipped bkit registry, install-state-independent, rather than keying it on the installed provider set the issue body asked for
description:
BKIT_SHIPPED_NETWORK_DOMAINS and the new BKIT_SHIPPED_NETWORK_HOSTS are module-init constants computed from the whole BKIT_EGRESS_SOURCES table, not from package.json bkit.opencodeProviders. Every consumer carries every registry host regardless of which provider they installed.
- **Current (checked 2026-09-23):** Rationale reason (1) no longer applies — the `SHIPPED_NETWORK_BASES` array was deleted (see `381-delete-cursor-hook-fallback-list-not-codegen`). Reasons (2) and (3) carry the decision.
rationale: Three reasons in order of weight. (1) Hash gating: the SHIPPED_NETWORK_BASES array sits inside the guardrails.cjs managed block, and markered-text means byte-equal on that block, so install-state-varying content there breaks bkit check for every consumer. Note the format changed from byte-equal-text to markered-text in #422; the constraint survives on the managed block, not on the whole file, and the original citation is stale. (2) The cloud allowlist is human-mediated: it is pasted into a vendor dashboard by hand and nothing in the toolchain can detect a stale paste, so a static list is pasted once and survives every later provider switch, whereas a reactive list goes stale the moment the consumer adds a provider. (3) The security delta is thin: an egress allowlist gates host reachability, not credentials, so carrying ollama.com on a repo that installed openrouter costs nothing because no OLLAMA_API_KEY exists to use it. The issue body's deterministic-and-reactive requirement is met by a stronger property: the host is reachable BEFORE the install rather than after it, and switching provider needs no re-paste.
alternatives: key on bkit.opencodeProviders as the issue body literally asked (rejected: cannot feed the hash-gated hook block, forces cwd threading through the constant's downstreams, and makes the pasted cloud allowlist stale on every provider change); a two-tier static-floor plus reactive-ceiling hybrid (rejected on shape not feasibility: .claude/cloud.md is untracked and .cursor/allowlist.json is a generated manifest entry, so it WOULD pass bkit check, but it creates a permanent per-surface asymmetry that must be re-litigated per surface and reintroduces the re-paste treadmill)

summary: delete the SHIPPED_NETWORK_BASES fallback array from guardrails.cjs outright and make .cursor/allowlist.json the sole source, rather than generating the array at build time or keeping it hand-synced behind a parity test
description:
loadNetworkAllowlistBases starts from an empty Set and reads .cursor/allowlist.json alone. An empty set makes curlWgetHostAllowed return false for any parseable URL, so the hook ASKS. The ask message names .cursor/allowlist.json and bkit install so the degraded state is self-diagnosing. No two-entry safety floor is kept. The same doctrine is applied to the fourth copy: the WebFetch(domain:...) seed is emptied from .bkit/shared/.claude/settings.json, where it was already a stale partial subset that enrichClaudeSettingsAllows topped up invisibly.
- **Current (checked 2026-09-23):** The pre-existing `.bkit/core/engine/install/modules/index.integration.test.ts` was kept and inverted, not deleted: it now asserts the hook carries no host list of its own and the shipped Claude settings seed no host grants.
rationale: Codegen recreates the exact failure this change exists to remove: a build step that can silently not run, leaving two copies drifting, and it couples a hash-gated shipped artifact to build ordering. A parity test automates the sync rather than eliminating it. The parity check that already existed for this pair (hook base list vs the WebFetch seed) was weak: both sides were hand-kept copies, so it could only catch the two drifting apart, never either drifting from the registry both claimed to mirror; its assertion is replaced, in the same test file, by checks that the hook holds no host list and the Claude settings template seeds no host grants (`.bkit/core/engine/install/modules/index.integration.test.ts`). Deletion is safe because the hook and the artifact are written in the same runCursorModule pass and under the same upgrade gate, so the artifact exists whenever the hook does; and because an empty set degrades to ask, which is the fail-safe direction #394 established (guessing here converts an ask into an allow). No two-entry floor: two entries is still a hand-maintained list that can rot, and the case it guards cannot occur, since the hook only exists because bkit install put it there in the pass that wrote the artifact.
alternatives: codegen the array into the hook at pnpm build (rejected: silent non-execution is the exact drift vector being removed); keep the copies and forbid drift with a parity test (rejected: does not satisfy the issue, leaves a multi-file edit per provider forever, and is the shape of the assertion being deleted); keep a minimal github.com plus npmjs.com safety floor so a fresh clone does not ask on everything (rejected: still a hand-maintained list, and the case is unreachable)

summary: The managed block (between `// bkit:start` / `// bkit:end`) of Cursor's bkit-gateguard.cjs is byte-identical to Claude's; the header comment and the consumer-owned driver around it differ
rationale: One advisory engine, two drivers; `gateguard-parity.integration.test.ts` asserts the blocks equal, never the whole files, because the drivers must differ to fit each host's payload and output contract. slop-scan disables `structure.duplicate-function-signatures` for these hooks because the blocks repeat by design.
description: Both hosts' managed blocks are generated from the same shared parts (`.bkit/core/hooks/gateguard-engine.js`, `.bkit/core/hooks/gateguard-edit-payload.js`) and are byte-identical. The rest of each file is host-specific: Cursor's driver resolves the workspace-relative `file_path` against `workspace_roots[0]`, emits `{ permission, additional_context | agent_message }`, and emits a bare allow on error; Claude's emits `hookSpecificOutput` and exits 0 on error. The files as a whole are not identical.

summary: GateGuard is advisory by default with deny behind BKIT_GATEGUARD=deny, fails open through one top-level catch, and keeps its managed block a pure engine with no stdin/stdout
description: GateGuard never blocks unless BKIT_GATEGUARD=deny. Normal control paths use existence guards; one top-level catch is the only error sink and exits 0 (Cursor: bare allow). The managed block reads no stdin and writes no stdout/stderr; the driver below it emits exactly once. Session-state GC runs after the advisory is decided. `.bkit/core/engine/audits/hooks/gateguard-parity.integration.test.ts` runs one behaviour table against every host.
rationale: The deny ramp is a deliberate, dogfood-gated flip: wired already so enabling it is a config change, not a code change. A hook that throws would break the consumer's session or stand between the agent and its edit. Two emitters (bkit's and the consumer's) on one stdout collide into one unparseable blob, which Cursor and Claude Code discard whole. GC runs last so a cleanup race cannot suppress the advisory. The parity table exists because getting the Codex tool name or the V4A envelope parser wrong leaves a hook that installs, exits 0 and silently never fires — a gate that proves only that it was asked. Reasons moved out of the hook comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).
alternatives: Deny by default — not adopted pending dogfood. Per-call try/catch — not adopted: one error sink only.

summary: Drift rules scan two partitioned surfaces, `product` and `tests`; a rule with no `surface` key scans `product`
description: `bkit-graph-drift.py` puts every scanned file on exactly one surface: `tests` = files under an `e2e` directory or named `.test.` / `.spec.`; `product` = everything else, test helpers included (`scripts/graphify/bkit-graph-drift.py:61-83`). A rule picks `product` (default), `tests` or `all` (`:18-19`, `:90-91`). Same in `.bkit/templates/scripts/graphify/bkit-graph-drift.py`.
rationale: The test surface is exactly the set of files the product scan skips, so adding it moved no file and changed no existing rule's count, and therefore none of their exact budgets; the `product` default keeps that true for any rule without a `surface` key (the deleted header text in 14e2a557). The test surface exists because guards live in test code, which a product-only scan cannot see (`scripts/graphify/bkit-graph-drift.py:88-91`).

summary: Analysis, status-hole and preflight signal rules: per-run failure delta, deferral discipline attribution, explicit MERGED-on-entry marker, orphan-step reporting, `web` context optional, context-fetch parser parity with the workflow awk, unnamed blocks exempt from provision pairing
description: `.bkit/core/engine/commands/analysis.ts` diffs cumulative failures per repo (clamped at 0) and computes the unjustified-deferral rate per (subagent, model) over folded entities. `.bkit/core/engine/checks/status-holes.ts` classifies MERGED_ON_ENTRY from the explicit marker, falling back to both worktree-setup and regression-guard absent, and reports orphan steps. `.bkit/core/engine/checks/before/context-fetch.ts` treats `web` as optional, parses markers like the bkit-debug awk, and skips unnamed blocks for provision pairing. `.bkit/core/engine/checks/before/files.ts` (`detectTier2TextDrift`) ignores comment lines in managed-block drift. `.bkit/core/engine/shared/egress.ts` is a pure-data leaf. `.bkit/core/engine/install/write.ts` deep-merge follows template key order. `.bkit/core/engine/install/version-file.ts` treats a missing hash as consumer-modified.
rationale: Testing cumulative failures absolutely marks every run after the first bug as an error run, so the regression reads 100% error at every size; a falling total after a fold is not an error run. The discipline rate is attribution, not a leaderboard: a high rate means either a prompt under-specifying when deferring is legal or a turn budget running out (an agent near maxTurns defers instead of finishing), which need different fixes. Keying MERGED_ON_ENTRY on the absence of merge-pr / deferred-sweep would reclassify a double-hole Path A/B run and report zero holes — inferring the path from the evidence under audit hides the worst cases. Comparing heading vs literal steps is a tautology; an orphan step is a real prose bug no gate covers. A blocking hole gate on a 25–65% holey corpus is noise that gets disabled (384-tier3-promotion). Nagging every consumer for a third-party search key is noise; the host's web tools are the fallback. A marker the awk accepts but the parser rejects is a block that runs while every advisory reports it absent. An unnamed block can never pair with a provision block and would nag unfixably. Comments carry no load, so annotating a block must not trip drift. Registry branching lives in the coverage-measured `.bkit/core/engine/install/cloud-env.ts`; a leaf with imports could create cycles. Consumer key order once put `git push --force*: deny` after the force-with-lease allow, silently denying a permitted command (#255 P2-10). Defaulting a missing hash to drift forces a conflict instead of a silent overwrite. Reasons moved out of code comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: The slop-scan plugin flags escape-hatch casts, ts-* suppression directives, skipped/focused tests and blanket lint disables; among casts the object-literal double cast weighs highest; per-rule next-line disables are not flagged
description: `.bkit/templates/scripts/slop/bkit-slop-type-suppression.mjs` emits `boundary/type-suppression` (double cast, any cast, ts-ignore / ts-nocheck / ts-expect-error) and `boundary/gate-suppression` (.skip / .only / x- / f-prefixed tests, blanket eslint disables). Per-hit weights, summed and capped at 10 per file: object-literal double cast 1.5, other double / any casts 1, ts-nocheck 2, ts-ignore 1.5, ts-expect-error 1; `.only` / f-prefix 2, `.skip` / x-prefix 1.5, blanket lint disable 1.5. It pins `meta.apiVersion`, omits `delta`, and evades its own pattern literals.
rationale: A cast or suppression at a boundary lets a renamed SDK field or changed signature compile clean and ship broken while the boundary test passes against the wrong shape; the directives suppress the very error a boundary test exists to surface. The object-literal double cast is the shape that shipped consumer-b #122 / PR #282 silently broken, so it weighs highest. Skipped tests and blanket disables are the same weaken-the-gate reflex for non-type gates; the targeted per-rule next-line form is the doctrine's sanctioned opt-out. apiVersion is pinned so an engine API bump fails loud instead of running against a mismatched contract. Casts err toward under-flagging: a nag, not a wedge. Reasons moved out of the plugin comments (owner rule 2026-10-10).

summary: #143 — live-test gates reconciled to current `dev` (skip rename, reuse the #203 `@live`/`test:live` vocabulary)
description:
- **Category:** agentic
- **Status:** active
- **Decision:** The #143 plan (4 sub-plans merged 2026-05-25) is built **adjusted to current `dev`**, not verbatim, because two things landed under it: (1) the `.agents/` → `.bkit/` layout move (DE-19, #160) — all plan paths/line-numbers are stale; (2) #203 already shipped the consumer CI/test taxonomy with a **different** vocabulary (`@live` tier, `test:live` suffix, `run_live` gate, `[force live]` marker, 4-job `bkit-tests-scope`/`bkit-tests`/`bkit-tests-live`/`bkit-tests-check` scaffold) than the plan assumed (`LIVE_API` flag, `@smoke` tag, `test:smoke` script). Two human-confirmed reductions: (A) **WS-1 script rename SKIPPED** — `typecheck`/`format:check`/`test` keep their names; all gates key on existing names; the atomic-or-red-CI rename + its manifest/CI/husky/template/dist/snapshot blast radius is not built (the exact "keep what's in dev" directive). (B) **Live vocabulary = reuse #203's `@live`/`test:live`** — Run Tests appends the existing `test:live` (+ `test:integration:live`/`test:e2e:live` when a consumer declares them); no `LIVE_API`/`@smoke`/`test:smoke` layer is added to bkit. What IS built is the #143 **workflow-gate core** (greenfield): the inline live-tier probe + `TEST_SCOPE` record, the plan non-mock mandate, the build empirical-verify e2e-live gate, and a redesigned debug loop (see DE-24) whose Run-Tests head reproduces against the live boundary and gates fail-then-pass, with a `SOAK` mode for unknown-cause bugs.
- **Why:** The rename was the plan's named top blast-radius risk and #203 already shipped a working naming/CI standard, so re-litigating it via a breaking rename throws away dev work for no functional gain. Reusing the `@live`/`test:live` vocabulary keeps one coherent convention in bkit instead of two overlapping live-test layers; the gates are vocabulary-agnostic (they probe for whatever live script the consumer declares). The `.bkit/` remap is mechanical.
- **Discarded:** (1) Verbatim plan execution — stale paths + a vocabulary clash with #203. (2) WS-1 probe-both rename (plan default B1=a) — still the full blast radius; declined under "keep what's in dev". (3) Ship `LIVE_API`/`@smoke`/`test:smoke` alongside #203's `@live`/`run_live` — two overlapping conventions; deferred to `pending.md` as a future unification (consumer-a adopted `LIVE_API`/`@smoke`, so the merge is consumer-side first).
- **Source:** human
- **Related:** #143, #203, #160, DE-19, DE-24, KN-23, example-org/consumer-a#399/#403/#422, `.bkit/core/workflows/bkit-{debug,build,plan}.md`, `.bkit/core/prompts/bkit-{plan-generate,plan-review-3,build-summary,debug-failure-diagnose,debug-failure-remediate,debug-summary,debug-failure-soak}.md`, `.bkit/workflows.md`, `docs/testing.md`
- **Current (checked 2026-10-14):** Holds: no script rename, no `LIVE_API` / `test:smoke` live layer in the workflows, `@live` stays the live tag. Mechanism replaced: Run Tests no longer appends `test:live` / `test:integration:live` / `test:e2e:live`; workflows run the deepest declared `bkit:gate:*` script via `bkit tests run` (`437-local-gates-are-named-bkit-gate-scripts`, `gate-chain-naming-and-unseeded-deeper-gates`). `/bkit-debug` Step 3 tries `bkit:gate:static-unit-integration-e2e-live` -> `bkit:gate:static-unit-integration-e2e` -> `bkit:gate:static-unit` (`[live=off]` drops the live candidate) and holds the run's `TEST_SCOPE`; live fail-then-pass is gated there. `/bkit-build` stops at `bkit:gate:static-unit-integration`, so the build e2e-live empirical-verify gate no longer exists.
