The existing router secrets move too: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY becomes BKIT_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and OPENCODE_PROVIDER_KEY becomes the provider's own BKIT_ name (BKIT_OPENCODE_API_KEY, BKIT_OPENROUTER_API_KEY or BKIT_OLLAMA_API_KEY). Tracker secrets are already BKIT_LINEAR_API_KEY / BKIT_JIRA_API_KEY (grill Q2). Renaming live router secrets needs a migration entry and upgrade advisory; detectCiRouterSecrets, .bkit/cloud.md and the context summary jobs field use the BKIT_ names. GitHub's built-in github.token is not a stored secret and is unaffected.
rationale: answered by owner: all vars used with bkit must live in .bkit/.env even if used elsewhere and start with BKIT_ (see .bkit/.env.example) — so BKIT_GH_TOKEN, BKIT_LINEAR_API_KEY, BKIT_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, BKIT_OPENAI_API_KEY etc. A bkit-only name also means an app's own OPENAI_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY never starts an agent job by accident.
alternatives: A — keep OPENAI_API_KEY (grill Q7) with a collision advisory and a jobs summary field; B — also require a BKIT_CODEX=true repo variable.

summary: bkit-cloud.yml starts only the agent job named by bkit.cloud.agent; other agents' secrets never start a job
description: The router's context job dispatches exactly one agent job: the one matching the recorded bkit.cloud.agent (claude, opencode or codex), and only when that agent's BKIT_ secret is set. Secrets for other agents are ignored, so two or three agents never pick up the same issue in one run. This supersedes grill Q9's additive jobs (every job whose secret is set starts) and removes the race tracked by deferral 397-dual-agent-same-run-double-ship-when-both-secrets-set. The context summary jobs field names the one dispatched job and why the others did not start.
rationale: answered by owner: C — start only the job that matches bkit.cloud.agent. With every bkit secret under a BKIT_ name copied from .bkit/.env (719-cloud-router-secrets-bkit-prefixed), several agent keys being set at once is the common case, so additive jobs would routinely double-ship.
alternatives: A — keep jobs additive and widen deferral 397-dual-agent-… (races persist); B — chain agent jobs with needs: so later agents no-op (deterministic; later agents still boot and cost tokens).

summary: bkit-cloud.yml recovers FID and issue id only through bkit fids parse, called the way the bkit workflows call it; no YAML regex or second parser on any ref
description: The router's context job gets the FID and issue id from the same engine command the bkit workflows use in Step 1: bkit fids parse (--marker / --branch on feat/** PRs, --prompt-file on the dev commit text), from node_modules/.bin/bkit. Every YAML FID or issue regex goes, including the dev commit-scope parse the design kept with a widened regex. Like a workflow, the parse runs in a checkout of the ref it parses, so on feat/** the context job checks out the PR head and fids parse reads that branch's .bkit/issues.jsonl feature row, not dev's.
rationale: answered by owner: we need to use the same bkit engine command as in workflows to get issue id.
alternatives: A — accept fids parse against dev's .bkit/issues.jsonl (branch fallback may resolve issue-less, no dispatch); C — keep a YAML branch fallback after fids parse (second parser).

summary: The Linear / Jira label and terminal read behind the cloud router is proven by recorded-fixture contract tests only; .bkit/cloud.md marks Linear / Jira router dispatch as not yet verified live
description: The build proves bkit issues fetch's labels and terminal facts for Linear and Jira with contract tests over recorded API replies, including a done-category state renamed away from Done. No live Linear workspace or Jira site check runs during the build. .bkit/cloud.md marks router dispatch under Linear / Jira as not yet verified live; a wrong labels shape in the real APIs reads as unreadable, so the router fails closed and silently never dispatches rather than dispatching falsely.
rationale: answered by owner: B — recorded-fixture contract tests only, no credentials needed for the build.
alternatives: A — live check against one Linear workspace and one Jira site with a bkit:auto issue in a started and a renamed done-category state (real SC2 evidence; needs both keys and test sites); C — live for Linear, fixtures for Jira.

summary: The Cursor sessionStart tracker guard HARD STOPs a Jira session when node_modules/.bin/bkit is absent; a live sessionStart dump during build decides whether a wait is needed
description: Under Jira the Cursor sessionStart guard needs node_modules/.bin/bkit; when the bin is absent it HARD STOPs (fail closed). During the build a live Cursor background agent dumps the sessionStart env and ls node_modules/.bin/bkit to show whether environment.json install finishes before sessionStart fires; if it does not, the guard switches to polling for the bin up to 30 s before the HARD STOP.
rationale: answered by owner: A — fail closed, with the install-vs-sessionStart ordering (spike C12 blocked) proven live during build.
alternatives: B — poll for the bin up to 30 s, then HARD STOP (tolerates a late install; adds start latency); C — 'not verified' context line when the bin is absent (sessions run; Jira guard silently skipped).

summary: apt packages stay unpinned inside the digest-pinned base image (Cursor Dockerfile, cloud setup, CI zsh)
description: The Cursor Dockerfile (curl, ca-certificates, xz-utils; git, jq, python3), the cloud setup's xz-utils and CI's zsh install with apt-get and no version. The base image is digest-pinned; apt-get update then installs the release's current packages, including its security updates. Two builds from one commit can get different package versions.
rationale: answered by owner: C. Ubuntu removes superseded package versions from its mirrors, so pkg=<version> pins break rebuilds of the shipped template with no consumer change, and a snapshot.ubuntu.com date is a second pin that no Renovate rule can move. Version-sensitive tools (node, gh, vale, jq in cloud setup, pnpm) are already pinned and checksummed outside apt.
alternatives: A: pin each package as pkg=<version> plus a Renovate customManagers rule (rebuild breaks when the mirror drops the version). B: install from snapshot.ubuntu.com at a fixed timestamp (frozen set, but the date goes stale with no bot to move it, and security updates stop).

summary: The build runs no live checks: the Cursor sessionStart dump (TASK 15) and the three codex dispatches (TASK 16) are dropped; the owner's own use after ship is the live check
description: No sandbox repo, BKIT_OPENAI_API_KEY or Cursor background environment is set up for the build. The build stops at the fixture tests, actionlint and the packed-tarball dogfood. Unverified until owner use: Cursor environment.json install finishing before sessionStart (Jira guard needs node_modules/.bin/bkit) and the openai/codex-action input names at the pinned SHA. .bkit/cloud.md marks the codex router job and the Cursor Jira guard as not yet verified live, alongside Linear / Jira router dispatch. A failure the owner reports is fixed through /bkit-debug.
rationale: answered by owner: defer — implement, the owner starts using it and reports back if it does not work.
alternatives: A — owner sandbox repo runs both checks during build; B — keep the codex check only (one repo + BKIT_OPENAI_API_KEY), drop the Cursor one.

summary: The Cursor sessionStart tracker guard HARD STOPs a Jira session when node_modules/.bin/bkit is absent; an owner report of a blocked Jira session decides whether a wait is needed
description: Under Jira the Cursor sessionStart guard needs node_modules/.bin/bkit; when the bin is absent it HARD STOPs (fail closed) naming the missing bin. No live sessionStart dump runs during build (719-live-checks-deferred-to-owner-use). If the owner reports Jira background sessions stopping on the missing bin, the guard switches to polling for the bin up to 30 s before the HARD STOP.
rationale: answered by owner: A — fail closed; the install-vs-sessionStart ordering (spike C12 blocked) is proven by owner use, not a build-time check.
alternatives: B — poll for the bin up to 30 s, then HARD STOP (tolerates a late install; adds start latency); C — 'not verified' context line when the bin is absent (sessions run; Jira guard silently skipped).
